2. **Stock Positioning and Near-Term Price Target:** Jo Bhakdi describes repositioning his portfolio ahead of earnings using short puts at the $375–$385 range and states he has largely exited those positions with slight to moderate gains. He is now targeting $400 as his near-term price target (one to two weeks), using a strategy of in-the-money short puts stacked at $380, $385, $390, and $400. He also mentions a potential run beyond all-time highs to $500 on a longer horizon, contingent on the Optimus catalyst.

## Humanoid Bots
1. **Optimus Production Start Announced for June–July 2026:** Jo Bhakdi highlights what he calls the "Optimus surprise" from the earnings call — an announcement that Optimus will go into live production as early as June, with July being his working estimate ("let's say July"), which he characterizes as approximately 90 days away. He describes this as Tesla likely seizing the "pole position in the world" in humanoid robotics.

2. **Optimus Gen 3 Described as Revolutionary:** In addition to the near-term production announcement, Jo Bhakdi references Optimus version 3 as a "revolutionary humanoid robot" and plans a dedicated video on the topic. He frames this as a separate, longer-term catalyst beyond the initial production ramp.

## Robotaxi
1. **Robotaxi Scaling Vagueness Viewed as Bullish Signal:** Jo Bhakdi notes that the earnings call lacked clear milestones or delineated scaling plans for the robotaxi business, which he says was exactly what he predicted and interprets positively. His reasoning is that Elon Musk becoming "less bombastic" and more conservative in public statements typically precedes execution, not failure — summarized by his analogy: "dogs that bark don't bite and dogs that don't bark bite."

## Market & Competition
1. **Amazon Parallel as Template for Tesla Recovery:** Jo Bhakdi draws a direct analogy between Tesla's current post-earnings drop and Amazon's prior earnings sell-off driven by high capex announcements, which he estimates was a drop of roughly 10–20%. Amazon subsequently recovered to all-time highs, and he argues Tesla will follow the same pattern. He attributes the market's behavior to irrationality about capex spending at frontier AI companies.

2. **AI Singularity Framing as Macro Context:** Jo Bhakdi argues that the broader market context — including the recent launch of ChatGPT 5.5, DeepSeek version 4, and Anthropic model updates — confirms that the world is "living through the singularity," making high-capex AI and robotics companies the primary beneficiaries. He explicitly rejects the "AI bubble" narrative he says he has argued against publicly since approximately a year prior.

Notable quotes and data:
- Auto gross margin: **19.2% actual vs. 17.5% expected**
- Capex guidance increase: **$20 billion → $25 billion**
- Optimus production start: **"as early as June, probably July"** — approximately 90 days from video publish date (April 24, 2026)
- Cybercab described as producing **"dozens and dozens every day"** at Giga Texas
- Near-term stock price target: **$400** (one to two week horizon)
- Longer-term stock price target: **$500+** (contingent on Optimus catalyst)
- Tesla stock described as entering earnings at **$389**, with short puts positioned at **$375, $380, $385**
- Tesla capex characterized as **~15% of competitor-level spending**
- "The market can stay irrational longer than you can stay liquid — eh, first of all, I'm pretty liquid. And second, this time I don't think so."
- "Look how they execute. Look how they execute space Starship... look how Tesla keeps absolutely killing all these little details. This machine is running better than ever before."

articles.title: Tesla Pioneer Alpha BREAKING NEWS & LIVE DISCUSSION
articles.body:
This video is a live session hosted by Jo Bhakdi on his "Pioneer Academy" channel, covering Tesla's robotaxi and Optimus trajectory, FSD readiness for scale, and the launch of a new structured investment bond product called "Tesla Plus 50" tied to the Pioneer Alpha portfolio. Jo argues that Tesla's earnings were strong and the post-earnings stock drop represents a buying opportunity, while also asserting that the robotaxi inflection point has already arrived and is being underappreciated by the market. The session also includes a wide-ranging discussion on AI-driven job displacement, Optimus deployment sequencing, and options strategy.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD 14.3 Sufficient for Scaling — Version 15 Not Required:** Jo argues that both Elon Musk and Ashok Elluswami have stated clearly that FSD version 14.3 is sufficient for scaling the robotaxi fleet and that version 15 is not a prerequisite. He notes that the current bottleneck is not safety but over-caution — the system is too conservative, creating inconvenience-related edge cases like driving in circles rather than genuine safety failures. Intermediate versions between 14.3 and version 15 are expected to address this. Version 15 is anticipated sometime in Q3 or Q4 2026.

2. **FSD 14.225 Deemed Not Ready — Edge Case Example Cited:** A Pioneer Academy member reported that FSD version 14.225 on a Model Y caused the vehicle to jerk and stop at an intersection when a car approached on a yellow/red light, requiring manual intervention. Jo acknowledges this version has known issues and that version 14.3 represents a meaningful improvement as a foundation for scaling.

## Robotaxi

1. **Unsupervised Robotaxi Fleet at 19 Vehicles Across Three Cities:** Jo reports that as of the session date, there are 19 unsupervised robotaxis operating, growing at roughly one per day (approximately 5% per day). The fleet is distributed as approximately 15 in Austin, and 2 each in Dallas and Houston. He notes the expansion to Dallas and Houston is significant and that the ramp accelerated following the Cybercab launch event at the end of March 2026.

2. **Robotaxi App Now Available for Android:** Jo briefly references news that the robotaxi app has been released for Android users, calling it an indicator that "this is all coming together" and stating he would not be surprised by further near-term announcements.

3. **Inflection Point Declared — Market Not Recognizing It:** Jo asserts that the robotaxi inflection point has already been reached and the market is failing to recognize it. He describes the growth from zero on January 20th to 19 units three months later as evidence of scaling on a low base. His stated "forcing function" target remains approximately 1,800–2,000 unsupervised robotaxis generating roughly 5% of Tesla's 2024 free cash flow annualized — a level he believes would trigger a major stock repricing without requiring earnings to actually double first.

4. **Cybercab Production Underway — Approximately 10 Units Per Day:** Jo states that Cybercabs are currently being produced at approximately 10 per day and questions what Tesla will do with them, suggesting something significant is in motion. He remains uncertain whether Tesla will ever sell Cybercabs directly to consumers, suggesting the economics of fleet ownership may make more sense for Tesla.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus Deployment Sequencing — Five-Stage Ladder:** Jo outlines a five-stage deployment ladder for humanoid robots. Stage one is household sales to early adopters who will pay for novelty and utility before cost-effectiveness is proven; he believes millions of units could be sold into homes in this phase. Stage two is industrial manufacturing with repetitive tasks. Stage three is mining and agricultural/forestry work. Stage four includes electricians, plumbers, painters, and nursing. Stage five encompasses highly complex tasks such as surgery, which he expects may take until approximately 2035 or beyond.

2. **Optimus Competitive Position — Tesla Likely Ahead Despite Silence:** Jo argues that Tesla's silence on Optimus capabilities reflects a deliberate strategy to prevent copying, not a lack of progress. He contends that given Tesla's capital, talent, and pressure on the project, Tesla is very likely at minimum in the top three humanoid robot programs globally and possibly significantly ahead. He draws a distinction from FSD: Optimus will face real competition, whereas FSD does not.

3. **Fleet Learning Advantage — Knowledge Replication Across All Units:** Jo emphasizes the compounding advantage of a large Optimus fleet where any skill learned by one robot can be replicated across the entire fleet. He frames this as a civilization-scale advantage and notes it is extremely difficult for people to develop intuition for how powerful this becomes at scale.

4. **Optimus Gen 3 Pre-Order Deals Anticipated:** In response to a question, Jo states he believes large companies will enter pilot deals with Tesla for Optimus before version 3 is formally revealed, provided it is "decently good." He sees these early pilot agreements with major corporations as an important near-term catalyst.

5. **Fast Food as an Early High-Value Deployment Vertical:** Jo highlights fast food — specifically citing McDonald's — as a Goldilocks deployment scenario for Optimus: labor cost savings, low worker engagement rates to replace, and a customer attraction effect. He believes companies could profit from Optimus deployment in fast food even before broader economic efficiency is fully established.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Model Y Running FSD 14.225 — Performance Concerns Noted:** A user reported operating a Model Y on FSD version 14.225, with the system exhibiting overly cautious and jerky behavior at intersections. Jo contextualizes this as a known limitation of that version and distinguishes it from the improvements introduced in version 14.3.

## Financials

1. **Tesla Earnings Characterized as Strong — Stock Reaction Described as Sentiment-Driven:** Jo states that Tesla's most recent earnings beat expectations, including positive surprises on automotive margins. He dismisses negative market reaction as driven by poor earnings call "vibes" and presentation rather than underlying business performance. He uses this disconnect as a bullish argument, likening it to buying a Ferrari at a discount because the salesman wore a dirty t-shirt.

2. **Pioneer Alpha Performance — 106% Since Inception, 17% Alpha Over Tesla YTD:** Jo reports Pioneer Alpha is up 106% since inception (approximately January 2024), Tesla is up 61% over the same period, and Pioneer Alpha has generated approximately 17% alpha over Tesla year-to-date in 2026. The portfolio is also reportedly up approximately 2% over the S&P 500 year-to-date, and approximately 57% above S&P 500 performance since inception.

3. **Pioneer Alpha Portfolio Composition:** Jo discloses his current holdings as: Tesla (largest position, with significant leverage), Nvidia (second position), MicroStrategy (third, as a Bitcoin proxy), and Robinhood (fourth). He uses options extensively around these positions, with a primary focus on Tesla short puts.

4. **New "Tesla Plus 50" Bond Product Launched:** Jo announces a new structured bond product called "Tesla Plus 50" via Pioneer Reserve (Luxembourg). The bond tracks Pioneer Alpha portfolio performance, capped at Tesla's performance as a benchmark, with investors receiving 100% of performance up to Tesla's return plus 50% of any outperformance above Tesla. If Pioneer Alpha underperforms Tesla, investors receive only Pioneer Alpha's return. There is downside risk with no capital protection, and a liquidation floor triggers if the portfolio drops more than 40% from initial principal. The bond has a 3-year maturity with 1.5% annual operating expenses (4.5% total over 3 years). Minimum investment is CHF/USD 25,000 (non-EU) or EUR 100,000 (EU). A stress test target of $1 million in the initial series is mentioned before launch.

5. **Near-Term Price Target of $400 for Tesla:** Jo states he believes Tesla could return to $400 within approximately two weeks, describing this as "more likely than not" given current positioning. He cites a technical upside target of $490 (all-time highs) as achievable without any major robotaxi catalyst, and states that reaching approximately 1,800–2,000 unsupervised robotaxis would trigger a repricing well above all-time highs.

## Market & Competition

1. **AI Job Displacement — Mass Replacement Expected by 2027:** Jo states his view that mass replacement of human workers by AI agents and robots will be clearly visible by 2027, which he calls "an absolute storm." He identifies sectors facing near-term wipeout as: junior/mid-level legal and banking roles, HR, healthcare administration, standard software coding, and sales. He criticizes corporate narratives suggesting workers can simply "learn AI" and keep their jobs as "the biggest gaslighting operation" he has seen.

2. **Autonomy TAM Framed as Multi-Trillion Dollar Market:** In response to a question about whether autonomy TAM is overvalued, Jo argues the addressable market includes global trucking (approximately $4 trillion), car ownership (estimated at approximately $5–6 trillion), and public transport, making total transportation a $10 trillion-plus market. He contends ride-sharing will expand significantly as it cannibalizes car ownership.

3. **Exponential AI Competitive Landscape — Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek:** Jo references Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT, and DeepSeek version 4 as converging rapidly alongside Optimus and robotaxi, creating compounding disruption. He specifically notes that Anthropic's launch of Claude Code and Claude Design has begun displacing existing design software sectors in real time, including previously favored tools like Lovable.

Notable quotes and data:
- "We are at 19 [unsupervised robotaxis]. It goes up one per day right now. It goes up like 5% a day."
- "15 in Austin... 4 in Dallas and Houston" (2 each)
- Robotaxi fleet started at zero on January 20th (2026); now at 19 approximately 3 months later
- "Cybercabs coming out... churning out like 10 Cybercabs a day"
- FSD version 15 anticipated in "Q3 maybe Q4" 2026
- Forcing function target: ~1,800–2,000 unsupervised robotaxis generating ~5% of 2024 free cash flow annualized
- Pioneer Alpha up 106% since inception (January 2024), Tesla up 61% same period
- Pioneer Alpha up ~17% alpha over Tesla year-to-date 2026; ~57% above S&P since inception
- Tesla Plus 50 bond: 3-year maturity, 1.5%/year operating expenses, min $25K (non-EU) / €100K (EU), liquidation floor at 40% drawdown
- "I think 2027 will be a wild year" — mass panic on AI employment implications
- "I think we can short-term go to 400 in the next two weeks"
- Near-term Tesla technical target: $490; post-forcing-function target: $600–$800+
- Jo's long-term Tesla price target: $6,000 by 2030; $10,000 pushed out to end of 2031
- Personal portfolio: approximately 50% liquid net worth in Pioneer Alpha; portfolio is approximately 70%+ Tesla plus leverage

articles.title: Daily X Summary (2026-04-24)
articles.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts deliver a broad set of high-signal updates across Tesla's core investment thesis pillars: Cybercab production is visibly ramping at Giga Texas, FSD V14.3.2 is rolling out with notable improvements, and Tesla's earnings call surfaced strong subscriber and backlog data. A major AI hardware acquisition and an Optimus factory preparation timeline add further catalysts, while Giga Berlin's announced production ramp signals recovering EV demand in Europe.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **Cybercab Production Ramp Visibly Underway at Giga Texas:** Tesla released a new video showing Cybercabs *without steering wheels* rolling off the production line and driving themselves autonomously to the outbound lot — one of the clearest public confirmations yet that Cybercab manufacturing is live. Separately, glossy gold Cybercabs were spotted out and about at Giga Texas, adding to earlier sightings of matte variants. The no-steering-wheel detail is significant as it confirms Tesla is building the vehicle in its final, fully driverless configuration rather than a transitional prototype form. These posts generated strong engagement (3.6K likes / 310 RTs for the production line video), suggesting viral reach on a meaningful milestone.

2. **FSD V14.3.2 Rolling Out — Key Behavioral and UX Improvements:** FSD V14.3.2 is now in early user hands. Sawyer Merritt's first-drive report highlights that "Mad Max" highway mode no longer hugs the far-left lane and stayed below 80 mph throughout, describing the behavior as "perfect." Actually Smart Summon saw meaningful speed improvements in initiating pull-forward and back-out maneuvers in parking lots. A new UX feature prompts drivers to select a reason when they disengage FSD, presenting a structured menu of options — a data-collection mechanism that could accelerate training feedback loops. These are qualitative improvements; no specific intervention rate or safety metric numbers were cited.

3. **FSD Fleet Miles Reach New Milestone — 28.8M Miles/Day:** Tesla updated its FSD miles tracker to reflect a larger vehicle fleet and increased FSD usage. The fleet is now averaging **28.8 million miles per day** on FSD (Supervised), up from **14.4 million miles per day** a couple of months ago — a **doubling** in roughly 60 days. This equates to approximately **333 miles every second**. This is a critical data point for both safety validation and the autonomous driving investment thesis, as fleet miles are the primary input for training and regulatory confidence.

4. **FSD Subscribers and Revenue: 456K Active Monthly Users, $45M+/Month:** Tesla disclosed that it now has **456,000 active monthly FSD subscribers**, generating over **$45 million per month** in subscription revenue, which Sawyer calculates annualizes to approximately **$565 million per year**. Additionally, Tesla ended Q1 2026 with its highest Q1 order backlog in over two years, signaling demand recovery. These figures provide direct high-frequency revenue visibility for the FSD monetization leg of the thesis ahead of broader robotaxi deployment.

5. **Tesla Acquires AI Hardware Company for Up to $2 Billion:** Tesla announced an agreement to acquire an AI hardware company for **up to $2 billion** in Tesla common stock and equity awards. Approximately **$1.8 billion** of that total is subject to service conditions and/or performance milestones tied to the success of the acquired business. The identity of the company was not specified in the posts. This is a significant strategic move suggesting Tesla is vertically integrating deeper into AI chip/hardware, likely to reduce dependence on third-party suppliers and accelerate compute for FSD and Optimus development.

6. **Optimus Factory Preparations Underway; Walter Isaacson Bullish on Tesla/SpaceX Merger:** Tesla stated in its earnings report that preparations for its **first large-scale Optimus factory** will begin in 2026. Walter Isaacson added public commentary that "millions of Optimus robots and self-driving cars" will be more transformative than LLMs. Isaacson also stated his belief that Tesla and SpaceX will eventually merge, citing the "Terafab" collaboration and Musk's practice of moving engineers between companies — though this remains speculative commentary from an outside observer rather than any official announcement.

7. **Giga Berlin to Add 1,000 Jobs, Target 20% Production Increase by Q3 2026:** Tesla announced it will create **1,000 new jobs** at Giga Berlin by the **end of June 2026** to increase weekly production by approximately **20%** starting from **Q3 2026**. The decision is described as a direct response to increased demand for the Model Y. This is a concrete near-term production ramp signal for the European market.

8. **Model S Signature Edition — Legacy and Product Update:** Hagerty published an exclusive look at the new **2026 Model S Signature Edition**, the final version of the Model S nameplate. Only **3% of parts** are shared with the original 2012 Model S Signature; the new version is **375 lbs lighter** and **40% more efficient**. While primarily a product/heritage story, it signals Tesla continues investing in its premium sedan line.

9. **Supercharger ML Model Update — 9M Miles of Training Data:** Tesla is rolling out an updated machine learning model to better identify vehicles that intend to charge, reducing wait times at Superchargers. The model is trained on **9 million miles** of aggregated and anonymized vehicle trajectory data within Supercharger geofences. This is an infrastructure efficiency improvement relevant to both the current EV business and future robotaxi fleet charging logistics.

10. **Honda Retreating; Gene Munster Defends Tesla's Capex Step-Up:** On the competitive landscape, Honda is exiting the South Korean car market after 23 years, adding to its struggles in EVs and China — framed as evidence of traditional OEM competitive deterioration. Gene Munster argued that Tesla's **25% capex step-up** is bullish, not bearish, as it widens the gap between Tesla and other automakers who are cutting EV and autonomy investment.

---

## Signal Strength: **Strongly Bullish** — Multiple simultaneous high-conviction catalysts fired today: confirmed no-steering-wheel Cybercab production, doubling of FSD daily miles, strong FSD subscriber revenue, a $2B AI hardware acquisition, Optimus factory prep confirmation, and a Giga Berlin production ramp all point toward accelerating execution across Tesla's core thesis pillars.

articles.title: How Tesla Thinks Differently Than Wall Street
articles.body:
This video features host Herbert and guest Cern Basher, a chartered financial analyst and founder of Brilliant Advice wealth management, conducting a detailed line-by-line review of Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call transcript. Their core argument is that the market's negative reaction to the call was largely driven by misaligned expectations rather than any fundamental deterioration in Tesla's business, and that a careful reading of the actual transcript reveals a significantly more positive picture than Wall Street's initial response suggested. The discussion spans capex strategy, Cybercab production, robotaxi expansion, FSD adoption metrics, Terafab, hardware 3 upgrades, and Optimus — consistently framing Tesla's approach as long-term and structurally different from how most public companies communicate.

## Financials

1. **Capex Acceleration and Negative Free Cash Flow Guidance:** The CFO stated that Tesla ended Q1 with just over $1.4 billion in free cash flow and that current expectations for 2026 capex are over $25 billion. He explicitly warned that Tesla expects negative free cash flow for the remaining three quarters of the year as the company enters a "very big capital investment phase" lasting a couple of years. Cern Basher and Herbert both frame this as a positive signal, drawing comparisons to Amazon's historical willingness to run free cash flow negative during expansion phases, and noting that Tesla has historically underspent its stated capex targets, so actual spend could exceed $25 billion.

2. **Six Factories Ramping Simultaneously:** The CFO noted that Tesla is paying for six factories currently going into or coming into operation, with some already started and others coming online later in 2026. This context was offered to explain the magnitude of the capex commitment and its multi-year duration.

3. **Tesla's Capital Efficiency Advantage:** Both hosts emphasized that Tesla gets significantly more output per dollar of capex than most other large technology companies, framing the increased spend as more valuable than a comparable outlay from a competitor. This was cited as a distinguishing characteristic separating Tesla from other Mag 7 companies also increasing capex.

4. **FSD Subscription Revenue Proxy:** Cern Basher calculated that with 1.28 million paid FSD customers globally at $99/month, the implied annualized run rate would be approximately $380 million per quarter — coincidentally the same figure as Tesla's regulatory credit revenue in Q1. He clarified this is a proxy calculation assuming all subscribers pay the subscription rate, not Tesla's actual reported FSD revenue, since some users purchased FSD upfront with revenue recognized over time.

5. **Elon's Communication Style vs. Nvidia's Investor Relations:** The hosts contrasted Tesla's earnings calls unfavorably with Nvidia's approach, noting Nvidia provides specific revenue guidance for the following quarter and then consistently beats it by several billion dollars, while also providing gross margin ranges. Tesla provides neither, which creates expectation management problems with institutional investors and algorithmic trading systems that respond to CEO sentiment.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD Version 14.3 as the Last Architectural Piece for Unsupervised FSD:** Elon was quoted directly on the call saying "I think version 14.3 is the last piece of the puzzle for unsupervised FSD." He hedged with "I think" rather than stating it definitively. The hosts interpreted this as highly meaningful — meaning a new major version is not required before unsupervised FSD can be deployed at meaningful scale, and that the 14.3 series is already running in Austin, Dallas, and Houston unsupervised.

2. **Version 15 — Complete Architecture Overhaul Running on AI4:** Elon said version 15 would be a "complete overhaul of the software architecture" running on AI4 hardware, coming "hopefully later this year" but "certainly by early next year." He stated that at that point the focus would be on raising FSD safety above human safety levels by another magnitude. Ashok confirmed on the call that robotaxi operations in Austin, Dallas, and Houston would continue expanding on the 14.3 base "for a while" until version 15 lands. The hosts noted this is not a prerequisite for initial robotaxi scaling — only for what Elon referred to as "very large scale" global deployment.

3. **Operational Issues, Not Safety Issues, Are the Limiting Factor:** Elon explicitly stated on the call that "a lot of what limits wider deployment of robo taxi are actually not safety issues, but convenience issues" — specifically citing cases where the car gets "paranoid and gets stuck," including literal infinite loop scenarios where the car repeatedly routes to the same blocked road. Ashok confirmed zero safety incidents to date across the robotaxi fleet. Herbert interpreted this to mean that incremental point releases within the 14.3 series (such as adding reasoning to more driving scenarios beyond end-destination parking, where it was already applied in 14.3.1) could resolve these issues without waiting for version 15.

4. **FSD Adoption Reaching 1.28 Million Paid Customers:** The CFO reported nearly 1.3 million paid FSD customers globally at the end of Q1, with the bulk of Q1 growth coming from subscriptions rather than upfront purchases. Upfront purchases increased only 7% as Tesla removed the purchase option in some markets during Q1. Cern Basher calculated the fleetwide take rate at approximately 14% of all vehicles ever delivered (roughly 9.2 million cumulative deliveries), noting the true take rate on eligible active vehicles is likely closer to 15% or higher.

5. **Incremental FSD Take Rate Exceeding 50% in Q1:** Cern Basher's chart analysis showed that the incremental FSD take rate — the percentage of new subscribers relative to vehicles delivered in the quarter (approximately 358,000) — exceeded 50% in Q1 2026. He cautioned this is partly inflated by existing owners subscribing for the first time rather than all being new vehicle buyers, and also potentially spiked by the "last chance to buy" FSD before the purchase option was removed. He expects Q2 to normalize but still expects it to remain above the previous high of 26%.

6. **FSD Usage Per Subscriber Nearly Doubling Year-Over-Year:** Cern Basher presented a calculation showing that in Q1 2025, the average FSD subscriber drove approximately 11 miles per day on FSD. By Q1 2026, that figure had risen to over 18 miles per day — nearly double. He framed this as evidence that FSD is transitioning from an occasional feature to a primary driving mode for subscribers, corroborated by anecdotal reports of users running FSD for 80–100% of their miles.

7. **Hardware 3 Cannot Achieve Unsupervised FSD:** Elon confirmed on the call that hardware 3 "simply does not have the capability to achieve unsupervised FSD." Tesla's proposed solution includes offering a discounted trade-in for hardware 4 vehicles, and offering a hardware upgrade path involving replacement of both the computer and cameras. To execute upgrades efficiently, Tesla plans to set up micro-factories in major metropolitan areas rather than processing upgrades at service centers, which was described as too slow. In the interim, Tesla will release a distilled version of the V14 software for hardware 3 vehicles that includes all V14 features except unsupervised capability.

8. **FSD Regulatory Progress in Europe and China:** The CFO reported receiving FSD approval in the Netherlands, describing it as setting up "well for EU-wide approval later in Q2." Supervised FSD was stated to be going to Brussels for EU review in May. For China, partial approvals have been received, with broader approval targeted for Q3 (which the host interpreted as a July 1st target). Elon said unsupervised FSD and robotaxi in Europe is a goal but the timeline is "at the mercy of regulators" and he said he does not know the timeframe.

9. **Unsupervised FSD to Customer-Owned Vehicles — Geography-Locked Rollout:** Elon stated he expects unsupervised FSD to reach customer vehicles "probably in the fourth quarter," but clarified it would be rolled out gradually and geography-locked — meaning owners in areas already validated for the robotaxi service would be enabled for unsupervised FSD within that same geography first.

## Robotaxi

1. **Expansion to Dallas and Houston — Unsupervised with No Safety Driver:** The earnings call confirmed Tesla expanded its robotaxi service to Dallas and Houston using the same software running in the Bay Area (Austin). The hosts noted that both new city deployments launched with unsupervised vehicles — no safety driver present — which they framed as a meaningful positive signal given the prior expectation that Tesla would follow a graduated safety driver phase-in. The stated limiting factor for faster expansion is "rigorous validation," not safety incidents.

2. **Cybercab Production Start as the Leading Indicator for Fleet Size:** Both hosts converged on the view that Cybercab production rate is the most meaningful leading indicator for the eventual robotaxi fleet size, since there is no logical reason to produce Cybercabs and warehouse them. Herbert's personal estimate for total robotaxi fleet size by end of 2026 is 10,000–15,000 vehicles, which he described as consistent with his expectations prior to the earnings call. He derived this estimate by assuming roughly 20 cities, approximately 500+ Cybercabs per city.

3. **Robotaxi Revenue — "Not Super Material" in 2026, "Material in a Significant Way" in 2027:** Elon said on the call that "unsupervised FSD or robo taxi revenue would not be super material this year" but "I do think it'll be material, probably in a significant way next year." The hosts spent considerable time discussing the ambiguity of the word "material," with Cern Basher suggesting a standard accounting definition might be approximately 5% of revenue, while Herbert suggested $500 million might qualify, and others in the Tesla community may interpret the threshold differently.

4. **12 States Expansion Target for 2026 — Scale Definition Disputed:** Elon said Tesla would expand robotaxi to "probably a dozen states or more later this year." The hosts debated what this implies in terms of vehicle count, with Herbert arguing that 12 states likely means at least 20 cities (given California alone could have three or four metro areas, and Florida similarly), and that each city would likely have at least 500 Cybercabs, implying a total of approximately 10,000 vehicles — consistent with his prior estimate. The ambiguity of "large scale" versus "very large scale" versus "millions of cars" was identified as the central unresolved communication failure from the call.

5. **QA Fleet Deployed Across the Entire United States:** Ashok confirmed Tesla has "a pretty large QA fleet spread across all of the United States," including rural areas, using engineering prototype vehicles for validation before customer deployment. The hosts observed that sightings of Cybercab engineering prototypes in many cities and rural areas confirm active validation is underway nationwide.

6. **Hardware 3 Retrofit as a Robotaxi Fleet Expansion Tool:** The hosts speculated that Tesla's hardware 3 upgrade program could be structured as a financial incentive to funnel retrofitted vehicles into the robotaxi network — for example, by offering the upgrade at low or no upfront cost in exchange for a commitment to put the car in the robotaxi network for a certain number of hours per month, or by offering a reduced Tesla take rate (cited as an example: reducing Tesla's take from 35% to 20%) as an incentive for owners to contribute their vehicle to the fleet.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus Gen 3 Reveal Delayed to August — Not a Production Delay:** The hosts noted that the Optimus Gen 3 reveal, previously expected by April and repeatedly delayed, is now expected in August. Elon's stated rationale was that Tesla would show the robot "as close as possible to production" — meaning the delay in the reveal does not necessarily indicate a delay in production itself. Herbert characterized this framing as an important distinction that many community members missed when interpreting the delay negatively.

2. **Optimus Production Line Replacing S/X Line at Giga Texas:** The earnings call confirmed that Tesla is sunsetting the Model S and Model X production line and converting it to an Optimus production line. Groundbreaking for the Optimus factory on the Giga Texas campus was confirmed as having occurred. Elon addressed this on the call to set expectations around the transition timeline.

3. **No Production Volume Guidance for Optimus:** In contrast to prior earnings calls where Elon gave specific numbers (e.g., 5,000 robots by year-end), he stated on this call that it is "impossible to calculate" how many Optimus units would be produced by year-end. The hosts acknowledged this is frustrating but framed it as Elon responding to criticism for giving numbers he subsequently missed, noting the previous 5,000 target was not met.

4. **Cortex 2 Compute Cluster Ramp — Key for Optimus Development:** The catalyst checklist referenced in the video includes reaching 50% capacity on Cortex 2 as an important upcoming milestone, described as particularly relevant to Optimus development. No specific timeline was given.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Highest Q1 Order Backlog in Over Two Years:** The CFO stated that Tesla ended Q1 with its highest Q1 order backlog in over two years, framing demand as having meaningfully recovered. He cited rising gas prices as an additional tailwind, while noting that the order rate improvement had already begun before gas prices moved higher.

2. **Giga Berlin Record Output of 61,000 Units in Q1:** The CFO specifically highlighted Giga Berlin reaching a record output of over 61,000 units in Q1 2026, and stated that Tesla plans to continue growing volumes not just in Berlin but across all factories.

3. **Battery Pack Capacity as the Binding Production Constraint:** The CFO identified battery pack capacity (not battery cells themselves) as "the biggest limiter" to production volume growth, stating Tesla is "actively working on resolving that."

4. **Vehicle Production Ramp Across All Factories:** Elon stated on the call, "We'll be ramping up production of all vehicles in all factories to the best of our ability through the balance of this year." The CFO added that Tesla is focused on increasing overall production volume, with the Cybercab ramp described as starting slow and going "kind of exponential towards the end of the year."

5. **FSD Now Positioned as the Product; the Car is the Delivery Mechanism:** The CFO explicitly stated that Tesla has "evolved our vehicle sales strategy where we now emphasize FSD as the product and the vehicle is only the delivery mechanism." The hosts interpreted this as a significant strategic pivot, noting it also represents an elevated liability commitment — if FSD is the product being sold, Tesla faces greater accountability if it fails to deliver.

## Notable quotes and data:

- Elon (Q1 call): "I think version 14.3 is the last piece of the puzzle for unsupervised FSD."
- Elon (Q1 call): "I think probably unsupervised FSD or robo taxi revenue would not be super material this year... I do think it'll be material, it'll be material probably in a significant way next year."
- Ashok (Q1 call): "The version of robo taxi that's running in Austin, Dallas, and Houston... those are essentially 13/14.3 variants, and it's obviously safe."
- CFO (Q1 call): "We ended the quarter with the highest Q1 order backlog in over two years."
- CFO (Q1 call): "FSD now is a demand driver for Tesla's vehicles... the vehicle is only the delivery mechanism."
- CFO (Q1 call): "We ended the quarter with just over 1.4 billion [in free cash flow]... current expectation for 2026 is over 25 billion in capex."
- CFO (Q1 call): Negative free cash flow expected for the remaining three quarters of 2026.
- Giga Berlin: Record Q1 output of over 61,000 units.
- FSD paid customers: Nearly 1.3 million globally at end of Q1.
- FSD incremental take rate in Q1: Over 50% (new subscribers relative to vehicles delivered that quarter).
- FSD usage: Average subscriber driving approximately 18+ miles/day on FSD in Q1 2026, up from approximately 11 miles/day in Q1 2025.
- Cern Basher's FSD revenue proxy: 1.28 million subscribers × $99/month ≈ $380 million/quarter run rate.
- Hardware 3 retrofit cost estimate (host speculation, not confirmed by Tesla): $5,000–$7,000 per vehicle.
- Herbert's robotaxi fleet estimate for end of 2026: 10,000–15,000 Cybercabs.
- Tesla take rate on robotaxi (discussed speculatively): 35%, with possible incentive reduction to ~20% for hardware 3 owners who enter the fleet.
- 10 billion cumulative FSD miles milestone: Calculated by host to be reached approximately May 6, 2026.
- Version 15: Expected "hopefully later this year" or "certainly by early next year"; will run on AI4; complete software architecture overhaul.
- Terafab research fab: Located on Giga Texas campus; approximately $3 billion cost; capable of a few thousand wafers per month; intended for testing ideas. SpaceX to fund the initial phase of the full-scale Terafab (location not yet announced).

articles.title: Tesla offers 1 year of free Supercharging, claims ~40% premium for non-Tesla EVs
articles.body:
Tesla has reintroduced one year of free Supercharging for new Model 3 Premium and Performance orders in North America, while simultaneously claiming non-Tesla EV owners pay a "~40% premium" on the Supercharger network — a figure the article disputes.

## Electric Vehicles
1. **Free Supercharging returns for Model 3 Premium/Performance:** Tesla announced the incentive via X, applying it to custom orders (not just inventory) of the Model 3 Premium and Performance trims only — excluding the base Model 3. The author notes this mirrors previous free Supercharging promotions Tesla has run over the years and suggests the offer is targeted at trims where Tesla is experiencing softer demand relative to the Model Y.

## Market & Competition
1. **Tesla's "~40% premium" claim disputed:** Tesla claimed non-Tesla EVs pay a "~40% premium" at Superchargers, but the article's analysis puts the actual non-Tesla premium at 30–35%. In high-cost markets like Los Angeles at peak hours, non-members pay roughly $0.60/kWh versus $0.45/kWh for Tesla owners (~33% premium); during off-peak hours the gap narrows to as low as 23%. Non-Tesla owners can eliminate the premium entirely with a $12.99/month Supercharging Membership.

2. **Supercharger pricing context:** US Supercharger rates currently range from $0.30–$0.45/kWh at most stations, reaching $0.50–$0.60+ at peak in high-demand areas. Tesla cut rates roughly 7% in late 2024. Dynamic live pricing, piloted at ~10 California stations in May 2025, has since expanded to 550+ stations.

## Editorial Stance
The author argues free Supercharging is a modest perk worth roughly $120–260/year for typical home-charging owners, but potentially $600–1,500+ for those without home charging access. On the pricing claim, the author says Tesla is "stretching the numbers" but acknowledges the built-in Supercharger discount is a real and increasingly relevant competitive advantage as more automakers adopt NACS.

Notable quotes and data:
- Non-Tesla Supercharger premium: ~30–35% per article's analysis, vs. Tesla's claimed "~40%"
- Peak LA rates: ~$0.60/kWh (non-Tesla) vs. ~$0.45/kWh (Tesla owners)
- Off-peak gap: as low as 23%
- Non-Tesla Supercharging Membership: $12.99/month; breaks even at ~80–100 kWh/month
- Dynamic pricing now live at 550+ stations (expanded from ~10 California pilot stations, May 2025)
- Estimated annual Supercharging savings for typical owner: ~$120–260; for non-home-chargers: $600–1,500+
- Tesla cut Supercharger rates ~7% in late 2024

articles.title: The Most Unbelievable Rocket Launch In History
articles.body:
This video is a SpaceX-produced documentary following the development and testing of the Starship V3 rocket system, including the new Ship 39 and Booster 19 vehicles. The content covers the engineering philosophy, production infrastructure, static fire test campaigns, and the broader mission of making humanity multi-planetary. This transcript contains no Tesla-related content and is entirely focused on SpaceX's Starship program.

## Market & Competition
1. **Non-Tesla Content — SpaceX Starship Documentary:** This video is entirely unrelated to Tesla, autonomous driving, robotaxi deployment, Optimus, or any other Tesla Thesis topic. It documents SpaceX's Starship V3 development program, including static fire tests of Booster 19, the construction of Ship 39 (the first V3 ship), and the engineering lessons carried forward from Starship's V1 and V2 flight test campaigns. While SpaceX is an Elon Musk venture with some relevance to the broader Tesla investor universe, no Tesla-specific information, data, or analysis is presented in this transcript.

Notable quotes and data:
- "Version three is what I like to call the foundational design of Starship booster in the pad." — SpaceX engineer
- "It'll be the one that puts humans back on the moon. It'll be the ones that put the first bootprints and then city on Mars."
- SpaceX produced approximately 600 V2 Raptor engines before developing the V3 Raptor 3 engine.
- Star Factory is described as an "almost 1 million square ft facility" built to produce both ship and booster.
- Booster 18 suffered an explosion during nitrogen system pressurization testing; no propellants were on board and no one was injured.
- Booster 19's first 10-engine static fire achieved 2.135 seconds of engine run time before a pad-side abort.
- Booster 19's second static fire attempt (full 33-engine) aborted at T+1.88 seconds due to a sensor fault on a ramp manifold.
- Ship 36 anomaly involved a CPV explosion that destroyed both the rocket and significant test site infrastructure at Massey's; the site was offline for 10 months.
- Starship V3 ship is designed to reach orbit, stay on orbit for up to 48 hours, perform rendezvous with other ships, and conduct propellant transfers.
- It took five flights from Flight 1 to Flight 5 to successfully catch a booster with the "chopsticks" mechanic.

articles.title: Optimus Is Real And Tesla Just Proved It
articles.body:
This video features host Brian of Futureaza interviewing Joe Tegtmeyer, a drone videographer who provides aerial coverage of Giga Texas, in a tour of major construction developments at the Austin site. The core thesis is that Tesla's on-the-ground construction activity — particularly the new Optimus factory, Cortex 2 AI data center, and Advanced Technology Fab — represents concrete, verifiable proof that Tesla's autonomous and humanoid robot ambitions are real and on an aggressive timeline. A follow-up video covering Cybercab specifically is teased for the next day.

## Humanoid Bots
1. **Optimus Factory Construction Underway at Giga Texas North Campus:** A major new construction project at the north end of Giga Texas has been officially confirmed by Tesla during the earnings call as the dedicated Optimus factory, targeting a 10 million units per year run rate. Joe Tegtmeyer reports the site is approximately 2 million square feet in ground slab alone, with active foundation work including footings, rebar cages, and geoper drilling equipment compacting gravel into the ground for structural support. A large excavation pit — described as a "plus" shape, roughly 2–4 meters deep — has been observed in the middle of the building footprint, possibly analogous to robot base infrastructure seen in the main factory's body-in-white welding area. The construction is believed to be phased, with the south end showing a different edge profile than the north, and a large adjacent field potentially reserved for future expansion.

2. **Construction Timeline Points to 2027 Readiness:** Based on observed construction pace and comparison to other Giga Texas builds, Joe Tegtmeyer estimates the Optimus factory will take approximately 18–20 months to complete to the point of initial operations, placing readiness well into 2027. This timeline is noted to roughly align with Samsung's chip fab for AI5, suggesting coordinated supply chain planning.

3. **Cortex 2 AI Data Center Partially Operational, Serving as Optimus Training Hub:** Cortex 2, located adjacent to the cathode building, is described as twice the size and capacity of Cortex 1 on the south end of the main factory. It is already partially operational, being used for Optimus training. Six cooling towers are active and supplemented by trailer-based heat exchangers. The facility is framed as "Optimus University" — the place where the robot learns tasks through data collection and training. This is considered critical infrastructure to support the Fremont facility, where Model S/X lines are being converted for Optimus production, with Tesla indicating initial production could begin as early as fall 2026.

4. **Optimus Test Track Under Construction at Southwest of Site:** A new multi-loop test track is under construction at the far southwest of the Giga Texas site. It features a large outer oval, a smaller inner oval, a tighter pad with chicanes, and turnarounds at each end — described as significantly more versatile than the Fremont test track. Active trenching and pipe installation for water management is underway. Spray oil has been applied to driving surfaces to mark them. Paving is expected soon. There is speculation it could also serve as a Cybertruck off-road testing area.

## Robotaxi
1. **Cybercab Crash Testing Active at Giga Texas:** Extensive Cybercab crash testing is ongoing at the Giga Texas crash test facility (and also at Fremont), with the goal of certifying the Cybercab as a production vehicle rather than a prototype. Joe Tegtmeyer explains this is significant because achieving full vehicle certification means Tesla will not be constrained by a production cap (such as the 2,500-unit prototype limit), and can deploy the fleet as fast as vehicles can be built. The crash test facility is described as a critical enabler of fleet scaling.

2. **Cybercab Production Line Has No Body Bank Requirement:** Unlike the Model Y and Cybertruck lines, which use a "body bank" system — storing pre-built bodies until needed — the Cybercab production area does not require this inventory buffer. This means there is significant open space around the Cybercab production area that could be used for future expansion of that line.

3. **Cybercab Deep-Dive Video Teased:** Joe Tegtmeyer previously received special access to view the interior of the Cybercab unboxed assembly line at Giga Texas, including details he could not initially share. Those details have since been published, and a dedicated follow-up video covering everything about the Cybercab is planned for the following day.

## Energy
1. **~400 Megapacks Planned for Giga Texas to Support Cortex 2:** Cortex 2 alone is planned to have approximately 260 Megapacks, with an additional 140 already on site elsewhere at Giga Texas, totaling roughly 400 Megapacks across the campus. Each unit is identified as a Megapack 2XL rated at approximately 3.9 megawatts. The primary purpose is power quality — smoothing grid fluctuations to provide clean, stable power to AI computing infrastructure. Currently, only about half of the Cortex 2 Megapack allocation is installed, with the crane and pad prepared for the remainder.

2. **Tesla's Transformer Stockpile a Strategic Advantage:** Joe Tegtmeyer highlights that Tesla has been stockpiling electrical transformers for years, anticipating a supply shortage now affecting at least half of planned U.S. AI data centers. With approximately 200 additional transformers visible on the west side of the site, Tesla's forward procurement is described as a key differentiator allowing uninterrupted buildout of power systems and Megapack infrastructure while competitors face bottlenecks.

## Market & Competition
1. **Advanced Technology Fab (Joint Tesla/SpaceX Venture) Breaking Ground:** A new Advanced Technology Fab — described as a chip research and development facility and a joint venture between Tesla and SpaceX — is being prepared on land previously used as a contractor staging yard on the east side of Giga Texas. The investment is stated at approximately $3 billion. The footprint is estimated at around 2 million square feet. Soil sampling with six or more drilling rigs is actively underway to assess foundation requirements. This facility is explicitly distinguished from the separately planned Terafab, which is described as a different and much larger future project to be built elsewhere.

Notable quotes and data:
- Optimus factory target: 10 million units per year run rate
- Optimus factory ground slab: ~2 million square feet
- Construction timeline estimate: 18–20 months to initial readiness, "well into 2027"
- Cortex 2: twice the size and capacity of Cortex 1; already partially operational for Optimus training
- Cortex 2 Megapack target: ~260 units; total site target: ~400 Megapacks
- Each Megapack unit: Megapack 2XL, rated at ~3.9 megawatts
- Advanced Technology Fab investment: ~$3 billion; ~2 million square foot footprint; joint Tesla/SpaceX venture
- Terafab is separate from the Advanced Technology Fab and described as "much much larger"
- Fremont Model S/X lines being converted for Optimus production; initial production potentially starting "this fall" (fall 2026)
- Joe Tegtmeyer: "They are able to deploy the fleet as fast as they can build" — referring to Cybercab once crash certification is complete
- Samsung chip fab timeline for AI5 noted as roughly aligned with Optimus factory construction schedule

articles.title: Tesla’s Most Underrated Factory Is A Monster
articles.body:
This video covers a firsthand tour of Tesla's Megapack factory in Lathrop, California, led by YouTuber Brian of the "futureaza" channel. Brian brings along a small group of Patreon and channel members to tour the facility, and the video is structured as a roundtable recap of their impressions immediately after the visit. The core thesis is that Tesla's Megapack factory is a highly underrated, world-class manufacturing operation that represents enormous and growing value in Tesla's energy business.

## Energy

1. **Megapack Factory Tour in Lathrop, California:** Brian and a small group of channel members were granted a tour of Tesla's Megapack factory in Lathrop (referred to in the transcript as "Lyra"), California. The tour was facilitated by a Tesla contact named Rex, and guided by a Tesla employee named Ivy. The group notes that access to this facility is rare and not typically granted to the public, making the visit a notable event for the channel.

2. **Factory Efficiency and Utilization:** Tour participants were struck by how fully utilized and busy the factory floor was — there were no idle sections or unused corners of space. The factory was described as clean, well-organized, and efficient. Notably, the facility makes use of vertical space (the Z-axis), including multi-story configurations with elevators, partly to create safer pedestrian walkways and partly to maximize production density. A large automated painting line was highlighted as a particularly impressive visual — units enter one end of a tube-like system and emerge fully painted and ready to be sealed.

3. **Automation vs. Human Labor Mix:** Attendees noted that while there is significant automation present, the factory is not a "lights out" operation — there are plenty of human workers on the floor. The bottom of each inverter pack is inscribed with the phrase "Made on Earth by Humans," which prompted discussion about how that will be updated once Optimus robots are integrated into manufacturing.

4. **Continuous Innovation Culture:** Tour guide Ivy stated that "the only constant is change" when asked what impresses her most about the factory. Attendees confirmed that new production lines are regularly added every couple of months, echoing a broader Tesla manufacturing culture of constant iteration. This was compared to an anecdote from a maintenance worker at Giga Nevada who returned from three days off to find an entirely new production area had been set up in his absence.

5. **Megapack Unit Economics and Quality:** Mitch, a former financial executive and business owner in the tour group, highlighted the extraordinary value being produced — each Megapack unit is worth approximately $1.5 million, and Tesla contractually guarantees service levels for two years with hundreds of thousands of dollars in potential exposure per unit. He emphasized that the build quality is comparable to heavy-duty over-the-road trucking equipment, and that Tesla's position as a top-performing energy storage provider "makes perfect sense" after seeing the factory. He described it as "literally a trillion-dollar business."

6. **Battery Cell Sourcing — LFP, Not Nevada:** A key revelation from the tour was the clarification of battery cell sourcing. A previous tour guide at Giga Nevada had indicated that the Megapack cells come from Nevada, but this was confirmed to be incorrect during the Lathrop visit. The cells used in the Megapack are LFP (lithium iron phosphate) chemistry, not sourced from Giga Nevada. When asked who the LFP supplier is, tour guides declined to disclose the information. Brian noted that publicly available information he had previously seen may have been inaccurate, and he intends to investigate further using only public sources.

7. **Shanghai Megapack Factory Confirmed Operational:** During the tour, Tesla staff confirmed that the Shanghai Megapack factory is operational. This aligns with indications that had surfaced in February 2025. However, the output figures for the Shanghai facility were not disclosed. Attendees noted that the Shanghai factory is a second-generation facility and is expected to be larger and more advanced than the Lathrop factory, with one participant drawing an analogy to comparing Giga California to Giga Texas in terms of generational improvement.

8. **Additional Megapack Factories Coming Online:** Tour participants confirmed that two additional Megapack factories are described as "about to come online" and are expected to be larger and more capable than the Lathrop facility. No specific locations or timelines beyond Shanghai were named in the discussion.

9. **Tesla Fire Department On-Site:** The group noted the presence of a dedicated Tesla Fire Department at the Lathrop facility, which they found interesting but logical given the nature of large-scale battery manufacturing and storage on-site.

Notable quotes and data:
- Each Megapack unit is worth approximately **$1.5 million**, with **two-year contractual service guarantees** and hundreds of thousands of dollars in potential liability exposure per unit.
- Inverter packs are inscribed: **"Made on Earth by Humans"** — prompting speculation about future updates once Optimus is deployed in manufacturing.
- Tour guide Ivy's key quote: **"The only constant is change."**
- Megapack cells are **LFP chemistry**, not sourced from Giga Nevada — contrary to what a previous Giga Nevada tour guide had stated.
- The **Shanghai Megapack factory is confirmed operational** as of the tour date.
- **Two more Megapack factories** are described as "about to come online," expected to be larger and more advanced than Lathrop.
- Mitch's assessment: **"It's literally a trillion-dollar business."**

articles.title: What Tesla Cybercab Production Kickoff ACTUALLY Means
articles.body:
This video by Jo Bhakdi reacts to Tesla's announcement — made during or around the Q1 earnings call — that mass manufacturing of the Cybercab has officially begun at Giga Texas in Austin. The core thesis is that the start of production-level Cybercab manufacturing (visually distinguishable by a glossy finish versus earlier matte prototypes) represents a genuine inflection point in Tesla's robotaxi scaling trajectory, and that the bears and skeptics are missing what is hiding in plain sight. Jo Bhakdi argues that the combination of Cybercab rolling off the production line without steering wheels, FSD already being deemed safe enough by Elon Musk, and a plausible deployment math toward tens of thousands of units by year-end makes Tesla extremely bullish heading into Q2 2026.

## Robotaxi
1. **Cybercab Mass Production Has Officially Begun:** Jo Bhakdi highlights that as of Wednesday (around April 23, 2026), Tesla officially started mass manufacturing of the Cybercab at Giga Texas in Austin — transitioning from production pilots to real, mass-manufacturable units. The most visible signal of this transition is the finish: earlier prototype versions were matte, while the new production units are glossy. Drone footage captured by Joe Tegtmeyer at 1:00 p.m. on April 23rd in the Giga Texas outbound lot shows multiple production-spec Cybercabs in the parking lot with people gathered around them.

2. **No Steering Wheel Signals Robotaxi-Only Intent:** Jo Bhakdi systematically addresses three camps of interpretation for what Tesla will do with these vehicles. He dismisses the idea that units with steering wheels will be sold to consumers as driveable cars (calling it "slightly delusional"), and equally dismisses the idea of selling no-steering-wheel units directly to consumers. His firm conclusion is that units rolling off the line without functional steering wheels are intended exclusively for autonomous robotaxi deployment — and that the evidence is simply what is in front of everyone's eyes.

3. **Deployment Math: Tens of Thousands by Year-End:** Starting from an estimated production rate of 10 Cybercabs per day (approximately 70 per week, or roughly 210 per month in the first month), Jo Bhakdi projects that even at a conservative 50% monthly production increase, Tesla would reach over 1,000 units produced within four months, 1,000 units per month shortly after, 2,000 per month, and 3,000 per month by December — totaling over 10,000 deployed units by end of 2026. He characterizes this as "painfully slow" scaling, which is precisely the language Elon Musk used, and notes that "painfully slow" for Tesla likely means roughly half or a third the pace of the Cybertruck ramp, which itself was described as painfully slow.

4. **Planned Deployment Cities Cited:** Jo Bhakdi states that Cybercabs being produced are expected to be deployed across multiple cities, including Austin, Dallas, Houston, the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Florida, Georgia, Boston, and Chicago. His narrative suggests units will be physically positioned in these cities in May and June, then switched on for service as deployment readiness is confirmed.

5. **FSD Version Already Deemed Safe Enough:** Jo Bhakdi references Elon Musk's comments that the current version of FSD (referred to as version 14.3) has already cleared the safety bar — safety is no longer the obstacle. The remaining issues are described as convenience problems: vehicles being overly cautious, occasionally getting stuck in loops, or taking significantly longer than expected on certain rides. He characterizes these as solvable in a matter of months and notes they are improving incrementally week over week, making the path to commercial deployment a question of gradual software refinement rather than fundamental safety work.

## Humanoid Bots
1. **Optimus Full Production Launch in 90 Days:** Jo Bhakdi briefly mentions that the earnings call included an announcement that Optimus will enter full production within approximately 90 days (from the time of the video, approximately late April 2026). He states this timing coincides with his broader bull thesis for Tesla's stock and teases a dedicated follow-up video on Optimus.

## Market & Competition
1. **Bearish Sentiment Characterized as FUD at an Inflection Point:** Jo Bhakdi frames the post-earnings stock decline — driven in part by Tesla not providing concrete robotaxi deployment numbers on the call — as a false flag and fear, uncertainty, and doubt (FUD) entering the market precisely at what he believes is a genuine inflection point. He notes his own portfolio was up approximately 17% relative to Tesla for the year because he correctly anticipated weak Q1 performance and positioned accordingly, and is now rotating back to a bullish stance for Q2 2026.

## Financials
1. **Stock Price Targets Mentioned:** Jo Bhakdi expresses a near-term target of $400, followed by a move above all-time highs over the subsequent 90 days if the Cybercab ramp and Optimus launch proceed as expected. He also references a potential move to $500 or beyond within 90–120 days, contingent on these catalysts materializing. He notes Tesla was down approximately 10% for the year at the time of the video, while his own portfolio was up approximately 6% for the year.

Notable quotes and data:
- "Since Wednesday, these things are now rolling off the line. Not anymore as little pilots, not anymore as production pilots, but as the real mass manufacturable version of the Cybercab."
- "If they produce 10 per day, that is 300 per month. That means by the end of May, we have like 400 of these things... we would be at a [few] thousand by December, many thousands by December if you only produce 10 per day."
- "We are producing 10 of these things per day. We are going to produce 70 easily 70 per week. And if you produce 70 per week we are producing 210 per month in month one."
- "Elon confirmed that 14.3 the current version of FSD is already good enough... safety is not a problem anymore."
- "The only problem is that every 10th ride, every 20th ride, every 30th ride, someone is trapped in the Cybercab and it takes 40 minutes instead of 20."
- "We have 10 to 20,000 Cybercabs end of this year. And that is exactly painfully slow."
- "Optimus is going to get launched in full production very surprisingly in 90 days — that was announced in the earnings call."
- Drone footage by Joe Tegtmeyer captured at 1:00 p.m. on April 23, 2026 at Giga Texas outbound lot.
- Jo Bhakdi claims personal portfolio up ~6% for the year vs. Tesla down ~10%, a ~17% relative outperformance.

articles.title: Daily X Summary (2026-04-25)
articles.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts are headlined by two major Robotaxi-related developments: the official Android launch of the Tesla Robotaxi app and fresh Cybercab production imagery, both signaling that Tesla's commercial robotaxi rollout is actively progressing. Secondary themes include an Optimus camera patent publication hinting at Gen 3 development, a Samsung chip facility milestone in Taylor, Texas directly tied to Tesla's AI/FSD supply chain, and a Model 3 Supercharging incentive suggesting continued demand support efforts. Overall signal is bullish for Tesla's autonomous and robotics thesis.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **Tesla Robotaxi App Goes Live on Android + Cybercab Imagery Surfaces:** In what is arguably the most significant development of the day, the Tesla Robotaxi app officially launched for Android users (post [5], 2.7K likes, 329 retweets — high engagement indicating viral reach on a meaningful catalyst). A separate post [6] shared what appears to be new footage or imagery of a glossy Cybercab, suggesting vehicles are physically present and deployment-ready. Combined, these two posts represent a concrete commercial milestone: the consumer-facing ride-hailing interface is now publicly available on a second major mobile platform, lowering the friction for rider adoption as fleet deployment expands.

2. **Cybercab Production Has Begun — Merritt Claps Back at Skeptics:** Post [9] (7.3K likes, 621 retweets — the day's highest-engagement post) shows Merritt referencing an article that had apparently predicted Cybercab would never reach production, noting that Tesla started Cybercab production just 18 months after the article was published. This is a pointed, high-confidence statement that Cybercab production has commenced, framed as a vindication of Tesla's timeline. No specific production volumes or ramp rates are cited, but the tone and engagement suggest this is a notable milestone moment.

3. **Optimus Gen 3 Anticipation Builds via Patent Publication:** Post [10] highlights a newly published (though older-filed) Tesla patent application revealing the camera configuration inside Optimus's head. Merritt explicitly notes he looks forward to seeing changes in "Optimus version 3" and suggests that by the time V3 is unveiled, meaningful time will have elapsed since the prior generation. No specific reveal date is given, but the framing implies a V3 unveil is anticipated in the not-too-distant future. Posts [16] and [17] ("The robots are here" / "Autobots, roll out!") appear to reference Optimus-related visual content with strong engagement (2.3K–2.4K likes each), reinforcing the humanoid bot narrative.

4. **Samsung Taylor, Texas Chip Facility Reaches Equipment Move-In Milestone:** Post [13] reports that Samsung held an equipment move-in ceremony at its $37 billion chip manufacturing facility in Taylor, Texas today, formally installing chipmaking machines that will begin producing silicon for Tesla and other customers "later this year" (i.e., later in 2026). This is a direct supply chain catalyst for Tesla's FSD/AI hardware stack, as Samsung is a key chip supplier for Tesla's next-generation compute platforms.

5. **Model 3 Free Supercharging Promotion Signals Demand Support:** Post [1] notes Tesla is now offering one year of free Supercharging with all new Model 3 Premium and Model 3 Performance orders in the U.S. While not a major fundamental shift, this type of incentive typically signals Tesla is actively working to stimulate near-term delivery volume, a mild demand-side data point worth monitoring heading into Q2 2026 delivery numbers.

6. **Competition Watch — Zoox Airport Rides, Ford-Geely Tech Talks, Porsche EV Cayenne:** Zoox (Amazon) has begun testing employee robotaxi rides to/from Las Vegas International Airport with public expansion planned (post [12]), a reminder that the robotaxi competitive landscape is developing. Ford and Geely have held (now stalled) talks about licensing Chinese EV technology for U.S. use (post [8]), reflecting broader industry pressure on legacy OEMs. Porsche unveiled an all-electric Cayenne Coupé starting at $116,000, with up to 355 miles of range, 400kW peak charging, and 1,141 HP in top trim (post [15]) — a premium EV competitor, though in a different price segment than most Tesla models.

7. **Alyath "Tesla Semi as a Service" Campaign:** Post [11] notes that Alyath plans to unveil a bundled monthly OpEx model for fleet access to the Tesla Semi at ACT Expo on May 4, 2026, with a planned 90-day program including the truck, charging infrastructure, and integration services — no upfront capital required. This is a notable commercial deployment model for the Semi that could accelerate fleet adoption.

---

## Signal Strength: **Bullish** — The Android launch of the Tesla Robotaxi app and confirmation that Cybercab production has started are concrete, near-term execution milestones that directly advance the autonomous revenue thesis, while the Samsung chip facility move-in and Optimus Gen 3 anticipation add further medium-term catalysts.

articles.title: Tesla's ChatGPT Moment Is Coming In 2026
articles.body:
This video from brighterwithherbert argues that Tesla's integration of Grok as a true agentic AI inside its vehicles represents a coming "ChatGPT moment" for Tesla — a demand-driving feature that will make every Tesla owner a walking advertisement. The core thesis is that sometime in late 2026 to early 2027, Grok inside Tesla vehicles will evolve from a fancy voice command system into a genuine AI agent capable of anticipating needs, controlling the car, booking appointments, coordinating with Optimus robots, and running multi-step workflows autonomously. The host identifies the AI5 chip — recently taped out on April 15, 2026 — as the key hardware unlock enabling this transformation.

## Autonomous Driving
1. **Grok as a vehicle AI agent, not just FSD:** The video is careful to distinguish the agentic Grok thesis from Full Self-Driving. While FSD handles the physical driving layer, Grok is positioned as the conversational, planning, and orchestration layer on top — a "two brains, one car" architecture inspired by Daniel Kahneman's dual process model. Tesla's onboard chip handles System 1 (fast, instinctive driving decisions), while Grok handles System 2 (slow, deliberate reasoning, multi-step planning, and agentic tasks). The line between these two systems is expected to shift as chips and models improve.

2. **Hey Grok launched April 13, 2026 in the Spring 2026 update:** As of the video, Hey Grok has just shipped and some users are still receiving it. Current capabilities include setting destinations, adjusting routes, finding points of interest, setting location-based reminders, and choosing from 14 personality modes (including storyteller, therapist, romantic, and conspiracy). What it cannot yet do includes controlling climate, music, windows, or seats; running multi-step workflows; operating apps on screen; maintaining true memory across drives; or talking to Tesla service AI on the user's behalf.

## Humanoid Bots
1. **Optimus Gen 3 production start expected summer 2026:** The host notes that Optimus Gen 3 production is expected to begin in summer 2026, and frames this as the first time Grok will appear in a humanoid body. The same Grok brain that lives in the Tesla is envisioned to also live in Optimus — sharing memory, personality, voice, and context. An example given is Optimus notifying Grok in the car that the user is out of milk, while simultaneously bringing a forgotten charger out to the driveway.

2. **Embodied AGI as Elon Musk's stated vision:** Elon Musk's framework for Grok is described as "embodied AGI" — a single unified intelligence that exists across multiple physical and digital bodies simultaneously: the Tesla, the Optimus robot, the phone, the laptop, and the user's X account. All instances share memory, personality, and context. The host cites Elon's stated comparisons to Jarvis from Iron Man and the supercomputer from *The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy* as intentional UX design targets, not marketing language.

3. **Grok as the operating system for Tesla factories and robots:** Beyond consumer-facing use, Grok is described as the agent layer controlling software workflows inside Tesla factories — quality control, scheduling, inventory, and defect detection — while Optimus handles physical labor. The host frames this as a 5-to-10-year story being laid down now, with Grok serving as the operating system for the entire Tesla physical empire: cars, robots, factories, energy, and service.

## Electric Vehicles
1. **Agentic Grok as the primary demand driver for Tesla car sales:** The host's central argument is that the evolution of Grok into a true agent — one that books service appointments, picks up dinner, drops kids at school, and coordinates with a home robot — will become a more powerful demand driver than EV range or Autopilot ever was. The thesis is that once one Tesla owner demonstrates these capabilities to a friend, that friend orders a Tesla. This "viral demo" dynamic is compared to the moment ChatGPT went viral.

2. **AI4, AI4 Plus, and AI5 hardware roadmap for vehicles:** Current Tesla vehicles run the AI4 chip with roughly 16 GB of memory — sufficient for distilled, quantized versions of Grok for simple local tasks, but requiring cloud roundtrips for agentic reasoning, introducing latency of 3–4 seconds that "kills the agentic feel." Tesla announced an AI4 Plus FSD computer with more memory and compute, described as a bridge chip expected to ship in some new vehicles in late 2026. AI5, which was taped out on April 15, 2026, is the full unlock: 192 GB of memory (nine times AI4), 8–10x the compute, 5x the bandwidth, benchmarking at roughly Nvidia H100 inference performance. AI5 enables fully local agentic Grok with sub-second latency and no cloud dependency. Small numbers of AI5 are expected late 2026, with high volume in 2027. The Cybercab is identified as the most likely first vehicle to receive AI5.

## Market & Competition
1. **Grok leads benchmarks in voice and translation:** The host cites Grok's voice agent API as ranked first on the BigBench Audio benchmark for voice reasoning. Time-to-first-audio latency is stated as under 1 second, the lowest of any commercial voice agent. On speech-to-text accuracy, Grok's error rate is cited at 5%, compared to ElevenLabs at 12%, Deepgram at 13.5%, and AssemblyAI at 21%. On translation, Grok is described as operating at native level across dozens of languages, switching mid-conversation without user prompting.

2. **Colossus training cluster as a structural compute advantage:** Grok is trained on Colossus, described as the largest training cluster on Earth, currently at 555,000 GPUs and targeting 1 million GPUs by late 2026. The host frames this as a structural compute advantage over OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, and argues that while those competitors are not standing still, this scale of training infrastructure creates a durable edge.

3. **Bears case and key risks acknowledged:** The host steelmans several counterarguments: current Hey Grok is essentially "Siri with attitude" and not yet the killer feature; cloud-dependent agentic AI in moving vehicles suffers from latency, especially in tunnels, parking garages, or rural areas; privacy concerns arise from a car that listens, watches, and books appointments on the user's behalf; voice agents may be a fad (though the host dismisses this for the in-car context); AI agents transacting on the user's behalf face unresolved legal and liability frameworks; and Grok could fall behind rapidly advancing competitors.

Notable quotes and data:
- Grok speech-to-text error rate: 5% vs. ElevenLabs 12%, Deepgram 13.5%, AssemblyAI 21%
- Grok voice agent API ranked #1 on BigBench Audio benchmark; time-to-first-audio latency under 1 second
- AI5 specs: 192 GB memory (9x AI4), 8–10x compute, 5x bandwidth, benchmarks near Nvidia H100 inference performance
- AI5 tape-out date: April 15, 2026 (9 days before video publication)
- AI5 timeline: small numbers late 2026, high volume 2027
- Colossus: 555,000 GPUs currently, targeting 1 million by late 2026
- Hey Grok launched April 13, 2026 in Spring 2026 update with 14 personality modes
- Optimus Gen 3 production start: summer 2026
- Cybercab identified as most likely first vehicle to receive AI5
- "The viral moment is late 2026 to 2027. Q3 and Q4 2026 deliveries are the early read."
- Elon Musk's stated vision: Grok as Jarvis from Iron Man / supercomputer from *The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy* — "embodied AGI in your driveway"
- Hybrid agentic Grok on AI4 expected "this fall"; full local agentic on AI5 by 2027
- Grok 5 release watch: Q2 2026 per XAI announcements
