Today's posts centered on three meaningful signals for Tesla investors: a significant demand surge in South Korea, a regulatory win as NHTSA closed its Smart Summon investigation with no injuries or fatalities linked to the feature, and the unveiling of an updated Terafab website confirming a joint Tesla/SpaceX/xAI chip-building initiative. The overall tone is constructive, with demand data and regulatory clarity offsetting the usual bearish analyst noise.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **Tesla Dominates South Korea Auto Market in Q1 2026:** In a high-engagement post (5.1K likes, 1.1K reposts), Merritt highlighted that Tesla ranked as the #1 imported car brand in South Korea on a quarterly basis for the first time ever — displacing established players like BMW not just among EVs, but across all fuel types. Tesla registrations in March surged +330% year-over-year. This is a notable demand inflection in a historically import-competitive market and suggests Tesla's global demand recovery thesis may be gaining traction beyond its core Western markets.

The agency found that nearly all reported crashes involved only minor property-damage incidents, with zero injuries and zero fatalities linked to the feature. This is a meaningful regulatory clearing event for Tesla's autonomous and semi-autonomous feature portfolio, reducing one area of legal and reputational overhang and potentially smoothing the path for future autonomous feature approvals.

The stated ambition is to represent "the most epic chip-building effort ever," with the tagline aspiring toward being "a galactic civilization." While grandiose in framing, this is strategically relevant for Tesla investors as in-house chip production could reduce dependence on third-party suppliers (e.g., NVIDIA, Samsung) and support long-term FSD and Optimus compute cost reduction. This post drew 3.1K likes and 392 reposts, indicating meaningful community interest.

4. **JP Morgan Analyst Pushback — Bearish Noise, Not a New Signal:** Merritt pushed back on what appears to be renewed bearish commentary from JP Morgan analyst Ryan Brinkman, noting that Brinkman has maintained the same negative stance for roughly 10 years during which Tesla stock rose approximately 2,000%. Merritt also noted Brinkman's price target did not change and that his average return is -1.6%. No new specific price target or thesis change was disclosed in the post, making this primarily a sentiment/context note rather than a new actionable data point.

---

## Signal Strength: **Bullish** — The combination of a historic South Korea demand record (+330% YoY), a clean NHTSA regulatory outcome on Smart Summon, and the formalization of the Terafab chip initiative collectively strengthen multiple pillars of the Tesla long-term thesis with minimal negative offsets today.

2026-04-08.title: Intel's Terafab Move Nobody Saw Coming
2026-04-08.body:
This video features host Herbert (brighterwithherbert) in conversation with economist and tech entrepreneur Jo Bhakdi, discussing two major developments: Intel's announcement joining the Terafab semiconductor project alongside Tesla, SpaceX, and XAI, and a Wall Street Journal opinion piece arguing that SpaceX's Starship Heavy could revolutionize military warfare. The broader thesis is that Tesla and SpaceX are no longer merely investment opportunities but are evolving into strategic national assets spanning AI, chips, defense, energy, and space — and that most investors still dramatically underestimate this transformation.

## Market & Competition

1. **Intel Joins Terafab as a Major Strategic Partner:** Intel announced it is joining Terafab, the ambitious semiconductor manufacturing project being built by Tesla, SpaceX, and XAI. Intel's CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated the company will contribute capabilities in "designing, fabricating, and packaging ultra high performance chips at scale," and described the project as "a step change in how silicon logic, memory, and packaging will get built in the future." Terafab's stated goal is to produce one terawatt per year of compute to power advances in AI and robotics. Tesla itself announced that Terafab combines logic, memory, and advanced packaging under one roof — something described as never having been done before. A new Terafab website was also launched alongside the announcement.

2. **Why Intel Is the Right Partner — and Why It Needs Tesla:** Jo Bhakdi argues that Intel is the ideal partner precisely because it is in a weakened competitive position — having been beaten badly by Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom — and desperately needs a growth story. He suggests Tesla could potentially acquire Intel at some point given Intel's depressed valuation and engineering talent, though he notes Tesla has historically preferred targeted technology acquisitions (pointing to the approximately $1 billion acquisition of a German robotics factory) over large corporate buyouts. He previously noted Tesla had a chip supply relationship with Samsung, including a commitment to receive all output from Samsung's factory in Taylor, Texas and a planned second factory in Taylor, Texas — but frames the Intel partnership as superior from a national security standpoint, since relying on Taiwanese or Korean technology represents a strategic vulnerability.

3. **Terafab's Chip Design Paradigm Is Fundamentally Different from Nvidia's:** Jo Bhakdi argues that Terafab is not trying to compete with Nvidia on general-purpose GPU design, which he says would be a losing battle. Instead, the design target is radically different: producing chips optimized for inference at unlimited scale, eventually for deployment in space-based AI satellites where energy constraints on Earth no longer apply. He frames this as Elon Musk's core economic insight — identifying the one lever that changes everything — and argues that manufacturing unlimited chips at reasonable cost is actually a simpler engineering challenge than FSD, Optimus, or Starship, even if it is still enormously complex in absolute terms.

4. **Space AI Data Centers Projected to Undercut Terrestrial Costs by 2027:** Jo Bhakdi argues that once Starship's cost per kilogram to orbit falls below $200 — which he projects will happen in 2027 — space-based AI data centers will become cheaper than terrestrial ones. He describes this as a sudden inflection point where demand immediately shifts to space infrastructure. He frames this as an inevitable economic outcome: if AI demand is unlimited and space data centers are cheaper, all future data center investment flows to space. This is offered as a key justification for SpaceX needing an IPO now, with a cited figure of $75 billion in capital being raised — a portion of which would go directly into capex to manufacture thousands of Starships at scale.

5. **Tesla and SpaceX Merger Seen as Near-Certain:** Both Jo Bhakdi and Chamath Palihapitiya (played in a clip from the All-In Podcast) independently assign near-100% probability to Tesla and SpaceX eventually merging. Chamath put the odds at "99.999%," arguing that a SpaceX IPO would create an externally validated mark-to-market valuation that makes combining the companies financially and legally tractable, while eliminating shareholder complaints about Elon's time allocation across entities. Jo Bhakdi agrees, noting the two companies already exchange too many critical dependencies — SpaceX needing things from Tesla, Tesla needing things from SpaceX, and both needing XAI — to remain efficiently separate. He suggests the merged entity could be called "X Corp" or similar, referencing Elon Musk's longstanding X brand.

6. **SpaceX and StarShip Heavy as a Military Asset:** A Wall Street Journal opinion piece arguing that Starship Heavy could revolutionize warfare was discussed at length. The article describes a scenario where the US pre-positions conventional munitions — including kinetic weapons, bunker busters, cluster munitions, and fuel-air explosives with terminal guidance systems — in low Earth orbit for rapid deployment anywhere on Earth within minutes, without risk to American troops. The piece cites an estimated cost of approximately $100 per kilogram to orbit as the threshold that makes this cost-effective. It also argues that key Starship technologies should be treated as national secrets, and that leaking them to China should be treated as treason. Jo Bhakdi adds the strategic "higher ground doctrine" framing — historically, controlling the high ground (arrows, artillery, planes, rockets) has determined military outcomes, and SpaceX's lift advantage over any competitor is described as a factor of 100x to 1,000x for at least five to ten years.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus Manufacturing Scale Is the Core Challenge, Not Capability:** Jo Bhakdi draws a direct parallel between the Terafab chip manufacturing philosophy and Optimus: the real challenge is not building a robot that can do somersaults, but manufacturing 100 million and eventually one billion units. He argues that competitors showing off impressive individual robot movements are missing the point entirely — the only question that matters is whether you can manufacture at civilizational scale, and Elon Musk's companies are uniquely oriented around this framing.

## Market & Competition

1. **AGI as the Master Unlock Underlying All of This:** Jo Bhakdi argues that AGI — not Elon Musk, not Tesla, not SpaceX individually — is the real driver of the investment thesis. He states that the world crossed an AGI inflection point approximately three weeks prior to the recording (around mid-to-late March 2026), and that from this point forward, being even one month ahead of a competitor in AGI development could be decisive. He cites Nvidia's announcement of a humanoid robotics model (referred to as "Neo Claw" or "Nemo Claw" in the transcript) as evidence that major players are moving fast. He also notes that major institutional investors including Fidelity have publicly stated they understand the SpaceX space-AI thesis and are valuing SpaceX at approximately $2 trillion despite roughly $15 billion in revenue, suggesting the institutional money class has broadly accepted the strategic framing.

Notable quotes and data:
- Terafab's stated goal: produce **one terawatt per year of compute** to power AI and robotics
- Chamath on Tesla/SpaceX merger probability: **"99.999%"**
- Jo Bhakdi on merger: **"Something like 99.99%"**
- SpaceX cost-per-kilogram target: **under $200/kg by 2027** (Jo Bhakdi's projection)
- WSJ article threshold for cost-effective orbital munitions: **~$100/kg to orbit**
- SpaceX IPO capital raise cited: **$75 billion**
- Fidelity and large funds reportedly valuing SpaceX at **~$2 trillion** on ~$15 billion in revenue
- Anthropic cited as having hit a **$30 billion annual run rate**
- Intel described as approximately **$200 billion market cap** (Jo Bhakdi's rough estimate, unverified in the conversation)
- Samsung deal referenced: Tesla receives **all output** from Samsung's Taylor, Texas factory, with a second Taylor factory announced
- German robotics factory acquisition by Tesla referenced at approximately **$1 billion**
- Starlink cited as having approximately **10 million users** with V3 satellites coming
- Quote from Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan: *"Elon has a proven track record of reimagining entire industries. This is exactly what is needed in semiconductor manufacturing today."*
- Jo Bhakdi on Terafab: *"It's actually easy. I know people think I'm crazy when I say this, but it's ultimately an easy task compared to FSD, to Optimus, to Starship. This is the easiest thing."*
- Jo Bhakdi on the SpaceX/AI timing coincidence: *"On a 25-year time scale, this hits randomly something completely orthogonal, completely not even expected by Elon... it hits exactly that inflection point."*

2026-04-08.title: NEWS: Tesla DROPS FSD V14.3!
2026-04-08.body:
This live stream from the "brighterwithherbert" channel covers the release of FSD version 14.3, which dropped the night before the broadcast. Host Herbert is joined by David Moss — known for a coast-to-coast FSD drive — and Brian White from Future Aza, who collectively review early adopter reactions, real-world testing footage, and the implications of this release for Tesla's unsupervised robotaxi rollout. The core thesis is that FSD 14.3 represents a meaningful leap forward, particularly in reaction time and sign-reading capability, though it still falls short of the full "missing puzzle piece" milestone Elon Musk had implied.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD 14.3 Release Overview:** FSD version 14.3 dropped the night before the broadcast, approximately two days after Elon Musk had indicated it would arrive by end of week (Sunday). The release is described as going to a very small group of early testers — estimated at roughly 15 to 50 people outside Tesla employees — and is beginning to roll out more broadly. The panel notes that the majority of owners may never see 14.3 itself, and could instead receive version 14.3.1 or later as the first update they experience.

2. **Key Release Notes and Improvements:** The official release notes include: a 20% faster reaction time (attributed to a ground-up rewrite of the AI compiler and runtime); an upgraded reinforcement learning training stage; an upgraded neural network vision encoder with improved performance in low-visibility scenarios; fixes for unnecessary lane biasing and minor tailgating behaviors; increased decisiveness of parking lot spot selection; improved parking lot pin prediction; enhanced response to emergency vehicles, school buses, and right-of-way violators; improved handling of small animals; improved traffic light handling at complex intersections; improved handling of rare or unusual objects extending into the vehicle path; and improved handling of temporary system degradations.

3. **Upcoming Features Not Yet in 14.3:** Several anticipated features are listed as still forthcoming in future dot releases: expanded reasoning to all behaviors beyond destination handling (reasoning is currently limited to destination handling and stop lights), pothole avoidance, and improved driver monitoring system sensitivity with better eye gaze tracking and handling for hats and eyewear. The highly anticipated "Banish" feature (unsupervised parking/summon capability) is also absent from this release.

4. **20% Faster Reaction Time as the Headline Feature:** The panel identifies the 20% faster reaction time as the single most significant improvement in this release. David Moss demonstrated this live during his 10-hour testing session by jumping out from behind trash cans and poles at the last possible moment near the vehicle — the car stopped before Moss himself could register it was there, let alone apply the brake. A separate clip from the AI Driver account showed the car beginning to brake for a yellow light before the on-screen visualization had even updated, illustrating that the system's decision-making is now outpacing its own display rendering.

5. **Sign Reading and Reasoning Capability:** One of the most notable behavioral improvements cited was FSD 14.3's apparent ability to read and obey physical signs in contradiction to incorrect map data. A clip from Dirty Tesla (Chris) showed the system being directed by navigation to turn the wrong way into a parking lot marked with "Do Not Enter" signs — FSD overrode the map instruction, recognized the signs, and corrected its path. This was described by panel members as the clearest real-world demonstration yet of sign recognition being actively used in driving decisions.

6. **David Moss's 10-Hour Real-World Test in Dallas:** Moss tested FSD 14.3 for approximately 10 hours in Dallas, Texas, including a six-hour-plus live stream. Testing environments included areas near a baseball stadium with police activity (handled correctly in 2 out of 3 police encounter scenarios), a multi-story underground parking garage (successfully navigated entry, parking, and descent — though it attempted to exit the wrong way on a one-way road), sixth-floor parking garages (successfully navigated from top to bottom), SMU campus, back alleys near student housing, Dallas Airport, and downtown bar district street parking. Positive outcomes included smooth handling of a rabbit crossing the road at 2 a.m., successful multi-level garage navigation, and the ability to drive and maneuver with B-pillar and reverse cameras physically covered by testers.

7. **Persistent Issues and Regressions in 14.3:** Despite overall improvement, Moss noted several issues: infinite loops in parking scenarios (circled the same downtown Dallas block five times without attempting new strategies); difficulty with drive-throughs; one instance of refusing to proceed through a legal flashing red light at a large downtown intersection; navigating out of a one-way underground parking structure the wrong way; and parking quality described as potentially worse than 14.2 in terms of alignment (diagonal parking), though significantly faster. Blinkers were also noted to activate later than in previous versions.

8. **Comparative Assessment vs. Waymo:** Brian White and David Moss both contrasted Tesla's neural-net-first approach favorably against Waymo's rules-based architecture. They noted that Waymo has publicly announced a transition toward neural networks — which the panel interpreted as an implicit admission that its existing 15 years of rules-based code has hit a ceiling. A prior incident of a Waymo vehicle getting stuck in a puddle while other cars navigated around it was cited as an example of Waymo's inability to infer context the way FSD can. The panel also noted that Waymo already operates commercially despite getting stuck in loops, suggesting loops alone don't disqualify a system from deployment.

9. **Rollout Timing and Wide Release Expectations:** The panel discussed an unverified report that FSD 14.3 (or a 14.3.1 dot release) is expected to go wider on Thursday (April 10, 2026). Tesla AI reportedly signaled on social media that the highest-mileage FSD users would receive priority in the rollout. The panel consensus was that 14.3 is production-quality enough for wide release, with the 0.1 dot release expected to address brake-stabbing overfitting and minor regressions before the general fleet receives it.

## Robotaxi

1. **Unsupervised Robotaxi Readiness Assessment:** The panel debated whether FSD 14.3 is the version that unlocks faster unsupervised robotaxi scaling in Austin. David Moss's view is that FSD 14.2 was already capable enough for unsupervised operation in controlled environments, and that Tesla's delay is not software-limited but rather contingent on waiting for the Cybercab vehicle itself. He expressed confidence that 14.3 would support Banish-level unsupervised parking in environments like Costco or strip mall parking lots, but stopped short of endorsing broad urban unsupervised deployment.

2. **Dallas Robotaxi Depot Observed:** During his overnight testing session, Moss visited what appeared to be a Tesla robotaxi staging depot in Dallas, described as the same size as the known Austin depot — over 100 Model Y vehicles parked in a large lot with camera washers on-site. The panel noted these are likely destined for supervised FSD deployment, not unsupervised robotaxi operation.

3. **Texas DMV Regulatory Timeline:** A new regulatory development was flagged: the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles expects to begin accepting applications for authorization to operate automated vehicles on Texas roads beginning in early May 2026. Commercial operation of vehicles using an engaged automated driving system requires this authorization. Panel members expressed mild surprise that this framework wasn't already in place, calling it a logical and much-needed next step.

4. **European Regulatory Update Pending:** An announcement from the RDW (Dutch road authority) is expected on April 10, 2026, regarding FSD deployment authorization in the Netherlands and potentially broader European markets. The panel speculated that FSD 14.3's improvements — particularly the faster reaction time — could positively influence the outcome of that regulatory review.

Notable quotes and data:
- David Moss tested FSD 14.3 for approximately 10 hours in Dallas, including a 6-hour-15-minute live stream plus 3–4 hours of pre-stream testing.
- FSD 14.3 includes a **20% faster reaction time** from a ground-up rewrite of the AI compiler and runtime.
- Estimated **15 to 50 people** outside Tesla employees were testing 14.3 at the time of the broadcast.
- Dallas robotaxi depot observed with **100+ Model Y vehicles** and camera washers, described as the same scale as the Austin depot.
- Texas DMV expected to begin accepting AV authorization applications by **early May 2026**.
- Netherlands RDW announcement expected **April 10, 2026**.
- Unverified report that wider FSD 14.3 rollout may begin **Thursday, April 10, 2026**.
- David Moss: *"I think they're waiting just for Cybercab to put them out. That's why I think they're waiting."*
- David Moss on unsupervised readiness: *"Nothing safety related, nothing like that. Yeah, it's significantly better than 14.2 to sum it up."*
- Brian White on Waymo: *"Waymo is an embarrassment. I don't know if that's necessarily good enough."*
- On reasoning: *"Tesla AI said there is reasoning specifically with the stop lights, but they will be adding more reasoning as the dot releases go through."*

2026-04-08.title: Tesla Semi Breakthrough Leaves Freightliner Struggling To Keep Up
2026-04-08.body:
This video from the Futura channel features host Brian and guest Mark from "The Tesla Life" discussing the Freightliner eCascadia electric semi-truck as a direct competitor to the Tesla Semi. The core argument is that while the eCascadia is available today and has real-world mileage under its belt, it is significantly outclassed by the Tesla Semi in range, power, charging speed, and price — even before subsidies are factored in. The video also covers viewer Q&A and a "wrong answers only" segment from a previous episode.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Freightliner eCascadia Overview and Availability:** Daimler has opened orders for the eCascadia (Class 8) and the EM2 medium-duty truck. The Cascadia platform originally launched in 2007, with electrification beginning in 2019. Early test units were deployed to the Port of Long Beach and Penske in California. One customer, Schneider, now has over 100 trucks with over 10 million miles logged, making it a proven, commercially available product today.

2. **eCascadia Range and Charging Limitations:** The eCascadia comes in two battery configurations — 291 kWh and 438 kWh — offering 150 or approximately 230 miles of range respectively, with real-world averages closer to 155 and 200 miles. The truck uses CCS1 charging (established before modern megacharger standards existed), with a theoretical max of 270 kW using two plugs (realistically 250–255 kW) and 180 kW on a single plug. Charging from 10% to 80% takes as little as 90 minutes, which Brian characterizes as slow by current standards.

3. **eCascadia Power and Weight Trade-offs:** The eCascadia's power configurations range from 320 to 420 horsepower, with the largest battery, dual-axle version reaching approximately 480–490 horsepower — roughly half the horsepower of the Tesla Semi. However, the eCascadia is approximately 3,000 lbs lighter than the Tesla Semi, which is identified as one of its few meaningful advantages. It also supports sleeper cab configurations since it shares the existing Cascadia platform architecture.

4. **eCascadia Battery Chemistry and Supply Chain:** The eCascadia uses prismatic NMC batteries sourced from CATL, currently subject to a 25% import tariff. Daimler is partnering with ACT, Paccar, and Cummins to build a domestic battery plant to reduce reliance on imported cells.

5. **eCascadia Pricing vs. Tesla Semi:** The eCascadia costs between $400,000 and $500,000, with the national average for a Class 8 electric truck at approximately $411,000. California offers subsidies of $120,000 for road haulers and $150,000 for drayage trucks. By contrast, the Tesla Semi is expected to price between $240,000 and $260,000 — meaning that even with maximum California subsidies applied to the eCascadia, it likely remains more expensive than an unsubsidized Tesla Semi.

6. **eCascadia Safety Features and Autonomy Aspirations:** The eCascadia includes a full safety suite as standard — lane departure warning, traffic-aware cruise control to zero mph, and pedestrian avoidance — capable of tracking up to 40 objects simultaneously. Daimler has expressed intentions to have an autonomous trucking solution on the road by 2027, though no specific details about the program's progress are available.

7. **Tesla Semi Nevada Factory Status:** The Giga Nevada facility (referred to as the "Iowa West" plant in context of a separate footage source) is currently running a pilot line rather than full-scale production. Some near-complete prototype units have been run through the line to validate manufacturing processes, and those trucks are confirmed to be in the hands of shipping customers, indicating limited but real production output.

8. **eCascadia Six-Year Cost Savings vs. Tesla Semi Competitiveness:** Studies indicate the eCascadia saves approximately $160,000 in fuel and maintenance costs over the first six years compared to a diesel truck. However, Brian notes this still leaves it more expensive than a Tesla Semi over that same period, giving Tesla a structural cost advantage even without relying on subsidies.

## Market & Competition

1. **eCascadia's Core Competitive Disadvantage:** Brian summarizes the eCascadia's position bluntly: its only meaningful advantages over the Tesla Semi are that it is available today and that it is 3,000 lbs lighter (yielding more cargo capacity). On price, range, charging speed, and power, the Tesla Semi is superior in nearly every dimension. The video frames this as analogous to the Ford F-150 Lightning — an electrified version of an existing platform that minimized engineering risk but also limited performance potential.

2. **Tariff and Subsidy Dynamics Affecting Competition:** The removal of California EV freight subsidies (referenced via a viewer comment about DOJ/DOT actions against California's EV mandates) could disproportionately hurt legacy electric truck makers like Daimler, since the Tesla Semi's lower base price means it is more competitive on an unsubsidized basis. Outside California, where the bulk of trucking activity occurs, the eCascadia's cost disadvantage becomes even more pronounced.

3. **Infrastructure Lock-In Problem:** Brian notes that Freightliner built the largest semi-truck charging network based on CCS1 standards — but that early infrastructure commitment now creates a costly upgrade problem as faster and more capable charging standards have emerged. This is presented as a cautionary tale about first-mover disadvantages in rapidly evolving technology markets.

Notable quotes and data:
- eCascadia battery packs: 291 kWh and 438 kWh options
- Real-world range: ~155 miles (small pack) and ~200 miles (large pack)
- Charging: 10–80% in as little as 90 minutes; max ~270 kW theoretical on dual CCS1
- eCascadia horsepower: 320–420 hp standard; ~480–490 hp on large battery dual-axle variant
- Tesla Semi horsepower: approximately double the eCascadia's top configuration (implied ~960 hp)
- eCascadia price: $400,000–$500,000; national Class 8 EV average ~$411,000
- California subsidies: $120,000 (road hauler) / $150,000 (drayage)
- Tesla Semi expected price: $240,000–$260,000
- eCascadia is ~3,000 lbs lighter than the Tesla Semi
- Schneider: 1 customer, 100+ trucks, 10+ million miles logged
- eCascadia fuel/maintenance savings vs. diesel: ~$160,000 over 6 years
- Daimler autonomy target: on-road solution by 2027
- Brian event: Tesla Diner appearance April 18, 2026; Portland eCascadia/Tesla Semi presentation April 26, 2026

2026-04-08.title: Tesla AI Reaches the Point Where Everything Gets Decided
2026-04-08.body:
This video from the Futurazza channel features host Brian in conversation with a guest named John, who walks through a series of slides covering the rapid acceleration of AI capabilities — particularly in software development — and what it means for Tesla's broader AI thesis. The core argument is that AI has crossed a critical inflection point in early 2026, moving from a useful tool to a self-improving system, with profound implications for companies like Tesla that are building on top of these capabilities. The discussion is framed as Part 1 of a multi-part series, with Part 2 promised the following day.

## Autonomous Driving
1. **AI acceleration as the foundation for Tesla's FSD thesis:** The hosts frame the rapid improvement in AI coding and reasoning capabilities as directly relevant to Tesla's autonomous driving development. The comparison is made to Andrej Karpathy's (referred to in the transcript as "Andre Kopathy," corrected here) public posts from early March 2026, in which he noted that AI went from handling roughly 20% of his programming workload before Christmas to handling the majority of it within a matter of weeks. The hosts argue this same curve applies to the AI underpinning Full Self-Driving development.

2. **Anthropic's leaked next-generation model and its implications:** A private Anthropic blog post was accidentally made public, revealing details about a model described as approximately twice as capable as their current best released model (Opus 4.6). The hosts note this new model is reportedly so effective at finding software exploits that Anthropic pre-released it to cybersecurity firms before a general launch — analogized to Tesla's early FSD releases to testers. The implication is that the AI powering autonomous driving systems is on a similarly steep improvement curve.

## Humanoid Bots
1. **Self-improving AI loops as a parallel to Optimus development:** The hosts discuss Andrej Karpathy's "auto research" technique, in which a small AI model was wrapped in a harness that automatically tries modifications, measures results, and iterates — running loops every five minutes. Over two days, the system found 20 separate improvements on code that Karpathy, described as one of the best programmers in the world, had already fine-tuned. The hosts draw a parallel between this kind of self-improving loop and the kind of rapid capability gains Tesla would need to accelerate Optimus development.

## Market & Competition
1. **Claude Code versus Grok — the AI coding race:** The hosts discuss Claude Code (from Anthropic) as currently the leading AI coding tool, with the chief product officer of Anthropic reportedly stating that virtually 100% of their code is now being written by Claude Code — ahead of CEO Dario Amodei's earlier prediction of 90% within a year. Elon Musk and xAI's Grok are mentioned as pursuing a different philosophical approach: rather than instilling a "constitution" of rules (as Anthropic does), Musk is attempting to get Grok to understand the world on its own terms. The hosts note that Elon has said xAI will catch up, but express uncertainty about the timeline.

2. **AI productivity gains creating orders-of-magnitude software output:** The hosts highlight that a senior Anthropic engineer (Boris Churnney, identified as the creator of Claude Code) generated 229 pull requests — each representing a tested, mergeable piece of software — in a single month using Claude Code. This is contrasted with the traditional benchmark of a skilled software engineer writing 10 debugged lines of code per day in a complex codebase, illustrating what the hosts describe as orders-of-magnitude improvement in software development speed.

3. **AI at the inflection point — broader societal implications:** Referencing Dario Amodei's statement that "we have crossed the inflection point," the hosts argue that only roughly 10–15% of current AI capability has yet spread into the broader economy, because most AI improvement has so far been focused on writing software — the AI improving itself. The hosts suggest the remaining 85–90% of capability will cascade outward into other industries over time, with significant disruptive consequences.

Notable quotes and data:
- Andrej Karpathy (early March 2026): AI was doing ~20% of his programming before Christmas; it has since flipped to doing the majority.
- Karpathy's auto-research loop ran every 5 minutes and found 20 separate improvements over two days on already fine-tuned code, improving performance by an extra 15%.
- Anthropic CPO: ~100% of Anthropic's code is now written by Claude Code.
- Boris Churnney generated 229 pull requests in a single month using Claude Code.
- Anthropic's leaked next model is described as "twice as good" as Opus 4.6 but reportedly very expensive to run.
- Dario Amodei (Anthropic CEO): "We have crossed the inflection point."
- Hosts estimate only 10–15% of current AI capability has reached the broader economy so far.
- The video is Part 1 of a multi-part series; Part 2 was promised for the following day (around April 2, 2026).

2026-04-08.title: IRAN CEASEFIRE - Is This the Green Light for Tesla and AI Stocks?
2026-04-08.body:
This video from Jo Bhakdi's channel covers the geopolitical situation surrounding a U.S.-Iran ceasefire and its implications for investors in Tesla, Nvidia, and AI-related stocks. The core thesis is that the ceasefire — including a two-week negotiating window and Iran's new $2 million-per-vessel fee on Strait of Hormuz transit — significantly reduces tail risk for markets, and that investors should now shift back toward a "risk on" posture.

## Market & Competition

1. **Iran Ceasefire Reduces Market Risk:** Jo Bhakdi argues that the Trump administration's agreement to a two-week ceasefire with Iran — brokered in part through Pakistan — dramatically reduces the probability of further military escalation. He characterizes the shift in risk from roughly 50% chance of escalation down to less than 5%, citing the disciplined and formal tone of the official White House statement as a stark contrast to earlier inflammatory posts. He believes internal GOP pressure, from figures like JD Vance, Tucker Carlson, Joe Rogan, and others, was instrumental in forcing a de-escalation.

2. **Iran's Strait of Hormuz Fee as a Strategic Win:** A central element of the 10-point Iranian proposal — which Bhakdi says the U.S. has effectively accepted as a basis for negotiation — is Iran's right to charge a $2 million fee per vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with fees to be split with Oman. Bhakdi frames this as a significant diplomatic win for Iran, noting the arrangement is strategically elegant because splitting proceeds with the western-friendly Gulf Cooperation Council member Oman makes it appear more internationally defensible.

3. **Portfolio Repositioning Toward Risk-On:** Bhakdi describes having reduced his Tesla position when the stock was around $360–$365 as a deliberate de-risking move during peak geopolitical uncertainty, and notes that Tesla has returned to approximately $364 in post-market trading. He states he was previously leveraged around the $390 range and chose to exit. With risk now reduced, he says he is repositioning more aggressively — adding back Tesla, Nvidia, and MicroStrategy — while acknowledging he remains under his typical investment level of over 100% invested.

4. **Tesla and Nvidia Framing:** Bhakdi notes Tesla is currently around $364, well below what he describes as a prior peak of $480, suggesting roughly $120 of upside just to return to December levels. He describes Nvidia at approximately $183 as fundamentally undervalued relative to where it "should" be (citing $210–$220 as a fair target), and notes he shifted some allocation from Tesla to Nvidia during the crisis period because Nvidia was more fundamentally supported. He briefly mentions robotaxi as a potential catalyst for Tesla but does not elaborate.

5. **Crypto and Broader AI/Blockchain Thesis:** Bhakdi mentions Bitcoin at approximately $71,000 and notes that crypto held up well through the geopolitical turbulence. He frames Bitcoin and Ethereum as part of a broader AI and blockchain investment theme and suggests crypto is positioned for a significant run higher. He describes the overall market as a "coiled spring" with the geopolitical resistance that suppressed it now largely removed.

Notable quotes and data:
- "I decreased my risk 50% down to 5%" — referring to his estimated probability of further military escalation
- Tesla price referenced: approximately $364 post-market; prior peak cited at $480; prior peak in the recent rally cited at $380
- Nvidia price referenced: approximately $183; Bhakdi's target range cited as $210–$220
- Bitcoin price referenced: approximately $71,000
- Iran's proposed Strait of Hormuz fee: $2 million per vessel, to be split with Oman
- "The train is at $480. So we have $120 to go up before we even are where we were in December."
- Bhakdi reduced Tesla exposure when it was around $360–$365 and notes he is "pretty happy" to be back near that level

2026-04-08.title: Daily X Summary (2026-04-08)
2026-04-08.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts were dominated by the official release and first-drive impressions of FSD V14.3, a meaningful software milestone with multiple capability upgrades. Secondary signals include strong Tesla sales recovery in Germany, a new 420W solar panel deployment in Texas, Waymo's Nashville robotaxi launch (competitive context), and Intel joining the Terafab chip fabrication project alongside SpaceX and Tesla. Overall, the day's news skews bullish for the autonomy and product thesis.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **FSD V14.3 Released — Meaningful Capability Upgrade Across Parking, Highway, and Reasoning:** The day's highest-signal event was Tesla's official release of FSD V14.3, announced in a post that garnered 12.8K likes and 1.9K reposts — indicating significant viral reach on a material claim. Key new features include improved parking location pin prediction (now displayed on the map with a "P" icon), increased decisiveness in parking spot selection and maneuvering, and a rewritten component (the post was truncated, so full details are unavailable). First-drive impressions from Sawyer Merritt noted more comfortable highway follow distance, quicker acceleration from stop signs, and elimination of the lane-change hesitation observed in prior versions, though navigation routing was cited as still occasionally suboptimal. A notable behavioral detail: FSD V14.3 correctly avoided a handicap parking space and selected the next available spot, demonstrating improved contextual awareness. Tesla also appears to be testing a rollout prioritization model that favors users with the highest mileage percentage and total miles driven. Upcoming improvements telegraphed (not yet in V14.3) include pothole avoidance, expanded reasoning beyond destination handling to all behaviors, and enhanced driver monitoring sensitivity with better eye-gaze tracking, eyewear handling, and variable lighting accuracy.

2. **Waymo Launches Nashville Robotaxi Service — Competitive Benchmark:** Waymo officially launched public robotaxi rides in Nashville, Tennessee, adding another city to its expanding geofenced network. While this is a competitor milestone rather than a Tesla development, it is relevant context for Tesla investors tracking the pace of robotaxi market formation ahead of Tesla's own Cybercab deployment. It signals that regulatory pathways in new cities are opening, which could benefit Tesla's rollout timeline as well.

3. **Tesla Germany Sales Surge — Strongest March and Q1 on Record:** Tesla new car registrations in Germany jumped 315% year-over-year to 9,252 units in March 2026, per the KBA (Germany's Federal Motor Transport Authority). Q1 2026 registrations rose 160% YoY to 12,829 vehicles, the highest quarterly sales ever recorded for Tesla in Germany. This is a strong demand recovery signal in a key European market following the brand headwinds of early 2025, and suggests the Model Y refresh and/or pricing adjustments are gaining traction.

4. **Tesla's New 420W Solar Panel Makes First Installation in Texas:** The first installation of Tesla's new 420W solar panel was documented in Texas. This is a product milestone for Tesla's Energy segment, indicating the higher-wattage panel is moving from announcement to real-world deployment. No pricing or volume details were provided.

5. **Intel Joins Terafab — Chip Fabrication Project with SpaceX and Tesla:** Intel announced it is joining the Terafab project alongside SpaceX and Tesla, with the stated goal of producing 1 TW/year of computing capacity (post was truncated). Intel cited its ability to "design, fabricate, and package ultra-high-performance chips at scale" as its contribution. If accurate, this has long-term implications for Tesla's AI training and inference infrastructure, potentially reducing dependence on third-party chip suppliers and supporting the autonomous driving and Optimus compute stack. This is an early-stage signal and details remain limited due to the truncated post.

---

## Signal Strength: **Bullish** — The release of FSD V14.3 with tangible capability improvements, combined with record Germany sales and early Terafab chip partnership news, collectively reinforce progress across Tesla's core autonomy and demand thesis.

2026-04-09.title: Why Tesla Is Diverging From Legacy Auto
2026-04-09.body:
This video from "brighterwithherbert" features host Herbert and guest Brian White (of the YouTube channel Futurazza) discussing the growing crisis among legacy automakers — Toyota, Ford, and Honda — in the face of China's rapid EV advancement, and why Tesla appears to be diverging positively from this trend. The core thesis is that legacy automakers failed to invest seriously in electrification and vertical integration, leaving them vulnerable to Chinese competitors, while Tesla's tech-forward approach and manufacturing strategy have positioned it for continued growth across global markets.

## Market & Competition

1. **Toyota CEO Sounds the Alarm:** Toyota CEO Koji Sato addressed 484 suppliers at a summit in March, warning that "unless things change, we will not survive" and calling for a "sense of crisis." He cited rapid industry shifts, Chinese competitor speed in EVs, and software as existential threats, urging suppliers to boost productivity, reduce waste, and relax cosmetic quality standards to match China's pace. Brian White noted that while Toyota isn't yet in acute crisis, they are proactively looking ahead rather than waiting for conditions to deteriorate — though he pointed out that until recently, the best electric Toyota ever made still wasn't as capable as a 2012 Model S.

2. **Ford CEO Warns of Chinese Overcapacity:** Ford CEO Jim Farley stated in a CBS Sunday Morning interview that China's existing auto factories have enough capacity to serve the entire North American market and could "put us all out of business." He compared China's EV surge to Japan's 1980s automotive rise but described it as being "on steroids," citing advanced tech, quality, scale, overcapacity, and export pressures. Brian White noted that Ford's reliance on outsourced and overseas parts — with even the F-150 being only about 45% North American-built — leaves it structurally unable to compete, and that Ford's lobbying to block Chinese factories from entering the US is at odds with its own supply chain dependencies.

3. **Honda CEO: "We Have No Chance Against This":** Honda's president visited an auto supplier factory in Shanghai and, upon returning to Japan, told his own suppliers they must act quickly. Honda's China sales fell for the fifth consecutive year in 2025, collapsing from a peak of 1.62 million units to only 640,000. The company cancelled two planned EVs — the Zero SUV and Zero Sedan — along with the Acura SRSX revival, booking up to $15.8 billion in losses. Brian White noted Honda is operating at only about half its manufacturing capacity utilization in China, which causes significant financial bleeding due to lost economies of scale.

4. **China's EV Strategy as a National Priority:** Brian White explained that China's success in EVs stems from a deliberate, centrally planned decision to pursue electrification as a national security and competitive advantage. He noted that Chinese state manufacturers offer production line capacity to other companies on tight deadlines, creating urgency and speed that legacy Western automakers cannot match. He also pointed out that BYD sources approximately 80% of its parts in-house, giving it far more control, speed, and cost efficiency than Western automakers who rely heavily on outside suppliers. BYD's new factory alone is described as larger than all Tesla factories combined by a factor of two or three.

5. **Tesla's Competitive Divergence:** Brian White argued that the US government actually invested more per capita into electrification than China did, but only Tesla meaningfully took advantage of battery production credits, IRA credits, and price adjustments. He emphasized that Tesla's vertical integration and tech-first approach leave it in a fundamentally different position than Ford, GM, or Honda — noting that when Ford CEO Farley warns that Chinese automakers will "put us all out of business," that warning explicitly does not apply to Tesla.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Tesla Delivery Growth Across Key Markets:** Despite overall Q1 deliveries coming in below analyst expectations — partly due to factory shutdowns to retool for the new Model Y — Tesla saw strong year-over-year growth in several markets. China deliveries rose 23.5% in Q1 compared to the prior year, with March volume specifically surging 46% from the previous month. Germany saw new car registrations quadruple in March, representing approximately 100 cars per day, in a broader German EV market that grew 16% with battery electric vehicles rising 66% to 70,000 registrations and capturing 24% market share. South Korea saw a 330% year-over-year increase in March, which Brian White highlighted as particularly exciting given it is a relatively new Tesla market dominated by Hyundai and Kia.

2. **Model Y Long Range Expansion:** Tesla introduced the Model Y Long Range (referred to as "Y L") variant in China and has begun exporting it to Australia, New Zealand, and eight additional countries added just recently, including Singapore, Japan, and Malaysia. Brian White expressed confidence that the vehicle will eventually reach all major markets, noting strong consumer interest despite the slightly larger form factor.

3. **Tesla Japan Expansion:** Tesla is performing well in Japan and is doubling its number of service centers in the country, indicating meaningful market commitment and growing consumer adoption even in a market dominated by domestic brands.

4. **Cybertruck Line Underutilization:** Brian White noted that the Cybertruck production line is "desperately underutilized," which he cited as a direct reason Tesla cannot reduce Cybertruck prices as aggressively as it might want to while maintaining margin — echoing the same economies-of-scale dynamics hurting Honda in China.

5. **Tech as the Decisive Purchase Driver:** The host shared an anecdote about his sister — a decades-long Mercedes and BMW loyalist who imports cars directly from German factories — switching to a Model Y Premium in Canada after witnessing Full Self-Driving in action. Brian White drew a parallel to the BlackBerry-to-smartphone transition, arguing that once consumers experience the functional advantages of Tesla's software and autonomy features, traditional luxury brand loyalty breaks down.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **NHTSA Closes Actually Smart Summon Investigation:** The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration closed its investigation into Tesla's Actually Smart Summon feature, finding that virtually all reported incidents involved minor property damage with zero injuries and zero fatalities linked to the feature. Out of millions of summon sessions, less than 1% resulted in any incident, and those incidents were primarily low-speed collisions with stationary objects like cart corrals or curbs. Brian White called the investigation a misuse of regulatory resources, noting that anyone who has used the feature would know the car operates at very conservative parking lot speeds.

Notable quotes and data:
- Toyota CEO Koji Sato: "Unless things change, we will not survive. I want everyone to acknowledge this sense of crisis." — delivered to 484 suppliers in March 2026
- Ford CEO Jim Farley: China has enough production capacity "to put us all out of business."
- Honda CEO (paraphrased): "We have no chance against this." — upon returning from visiting a Shanghai auto supplier factory
- Honda China sales: collapsed from a peak of 1.62 million units to 640,000 units; Honda at approximately 50% manufacturing utilization in China
- Honda booked up to $15.8 billion in losses after cancelling EVs

2026-04-09.title: AI Breakout or Breakdown Tesla's Biggest Moment Has Arrived
2026-04-09.body:
This video is a wide-ranging conversational discussion between host Brian and guest John Twig on the Futurazza channel, covering the rapid acceleration of AI development, the growing capabilities of AI agents and autonomous systems, and the societal implications of automation. The core thesis is that AI and robotics — including Optimus — are advancing at an extraordinary pace, and while this promises an "age of abundance," the transition poses serious social and economic challenges for displaced workers.

## Humanoid Bots
1. **Optimus as a Future General-Purpose Assistant:** John Twig argues that Optimus robots will not merely perform physical tasks like vacuuming or folding clothes, but will eventually serve as professor-level assistants capable of having full conversations, managing finances, and optimizing complex tasks. He envisions a future where an AI chip (referenced as an "AI5 chip," described as potentially 10 to 20 times faster) powers an Optimus unit at the office, handling everything from portfolio optimization to resource management on behalf of their owner.

2. **Virtual Optimus as a Digital Alternative:** The discussion introduces the concept of a "Virtual Optimus" — effectively an AI agent running as a digital assistant for those who cannot afford a physical Optimus robot. This is framed as a parallel to OpenClaw-style agents running on personal computers, suggesting Tesla or affiliated entities may pursue a software-based version of Optimus's functionality for broader accessibility.

3. **Optimus Allocation Dilemma — Factories vs. Care:** John raises a pointed ethical question about where early Optimus robots will be deployed. He notes the UK care system currently has roughly 100,000 unfilled caregiving roles, leaving elderly and disabled individuals with inadequate support. He argues that despite the humanitarian need, economic incentives will direct Optimus units to factories first — where productivity gains and profit are immediate — rather than to care settings, and questions whether benefits will trickle down without deliberate intervention.

4. **Optimus Pricing and Accessibility Concerns:** The conversation touches on Optimus pricing, with figures of $20,000 to $50,000 mentioned as the purchase range. The hosts express concern that early ownership will be concentrated among wealthy buyers who can acquire hundreds, thousands, or potentially millions of units, compounding economic inequality during the transitional period. The suggestion that people could rent out their Optimus to neighbors is dismissed as impractical if neighbors have no disposable income either.

## Market & Competition
1. **AI Agent Acceleration — Claude and OpenClaw:** The discussion highlights the rapid feature shipping pace of the Claude team (Anthropic), with significant new features released nearly every day. OpenClaw, an open-source project allowing AI agents to run persistently on a personal computer — waking every few seconds to seek tasks — is cited as a revolutionary development. Anthropic's commercial equivalent, Co-work for Windows, was among the recently shipped features. OpenAI has reportedly hired the creator of OpenClaw. All major AI companies are racing to deploy similar persistent agent systems.

2. **Grok's Development and XAI Founder Departures:** Elon Musk has stated that Grok will improve every week, and XAI has been simultaneously training three Grok models at once, with results expected over the following weeks and months. However, a significant development is flagged: all 11 co-founders of XAI (excluding Elon) have departed following the merger of XAI with X (formerly Twitter). Meta is reported to be offering packages worth $300 million over four years to recruit some of those departing developers. The hosts express uncertainty about what this means for XAI's trajectory, though they note the company has continued hiring.

3. **Google's TurboQuant Compression Breakthrough:** Google recently released a compression tool called TurboQuant, which compresses input and output tokens passing through large language models by six to eight times. The practical effect is that large data centers can now run models on roughly half the memory previously required, and processing speeds increase significantly. This is described as a meaningful near-term efficiency gain across the AI industry, not a model size reduction but a context window compression improvement.

4. **AI Replacing Jobs — RethinkX Analysis:** Research analyst Adam Dorr of RethinkX is cited as arguing that AI and robots will displace nearly all human jobs, representing one of the most respected forecasts in the space. The hosts use this as a backdrop to discuss the societal pain of displacement — particularly for truck drivers earning $50,000–$100,000 annually with mortgages — who are unlikely to transition easily into new economy roles, even as autonomous vehicles like Tesla Semi promise massive productivity gains.

Notable quotes and data:
- Optimus purchase price range mentioned: **$20,000 to $50,000**
- UK care system has approximately **100,000 unfilled caregiving jobs**
- XAI co-founders who have departed: **11 out of 11** (excluding Elon Musk)
- Meta reportedly offering departing XAI developers packages worth **$300 million over four years**
- Google's TurboQuant compresses model context by **6 to 8 times**, potentially halving data center memory requirements
- XAI is training **three Grok models simultaneously**
- Chris from Dirty Tesla gave Claude **$500 to invest**; the account ended at approximately **$9** before being closed
- Grok won a vending machine business simulation against competing AI models, though one model was found engaging in predatory pricing (doubling prices when competitors ran out of stock)
- "Real world AI is about video processing and creating video" — attributed to Elon Musk, explaining why image/video generation matters for cars and Optimus

2026-04-09.title: Tesla Sales Surge Worldwide While Intel Partnership Fuels Bigger Ambitions
2026-04-09.body:
This episode of Futurza features host Brian and co-host Herbert from Brighter discussing three major Tesla developments: Intel's partnership with Tesla and SpaceX on the Terafab chip manufacturing complex, the release of FSD version 14.3 and its implications for unsupervised robotaxi deployment, and a notable surge in Tesla vehicle sales across several international markets. The core thesis is that Tesla is systematically assembling the pieces — compute infrastructure, software maturity, and demand drivers — needed to transition from an EV company into a subscription-based autonomous mobility platform.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD 14.3 Released with 20% Faster Reaction Time:** Tesla released FSD version 14.3, which Tesla itself emphasized delivers a 20% faster reaction time. This improvement is framed as critical for safety and as the key enabler for scaling unsupervised robotaxi operations. The hosts note that achieving this required a full top-to-bottom rewrite of the system. Visualization and camera processing speed were also improved, allowing the vehicle to detect obstacles more rapidly.

2. **Reasoning Capabilities Added but Limited in Scope:** FSD 14.3 includes reasoning functionality, but it is currently focused narrowly on destination understanding — interpreting what actions to take upon arriving at a destination. Tesla indicated that broader reasoning capabilities will be released incrementally in future point releases. The hosts and their guest David Moss agreed this is not yet the reasoning breakthrough that would fully change the game for autonomous driving.

3. **David Moss Testing and Safety Validation:** Tester David Moss — known for performing coast-to-coast drives with FSD 14.2 and being featured in Tesla's own coverage — logged over 10 hours on FSD 14.3 before and after the live stream, with plans to do an additional 5 hours. Moss conducted back-alley pedestrian pop-out tests at night to evaluate reaction time, and the system demonstrated fast and reliable obstacle detection. Moss believes FSD 14.2 was already good enough for unsupervised robotaxi deployment, and that 14.3's safety improvements further reinforce that case.

4. **FSD Wide Release Imminent:** As of the time of recording, over 50 testers had evaluated FSD 14.3, and the consensus among them was that it is ready for wide release. Herbert views wide release as a significant demand driver for Tesla vehicles, citing a personal anecdote about a brand-loyal Mercedes/BMW driver who expressed interest in buying a Tesla after experiencing FSD firsthand.

## Robotaxi

1. **Unsupervised Deployment: A Choice, Not a Capability Gap:** The hosts argue that the gap between Tesla and Waymo on unsupervised robotaxi is not one of technical ability — it is a strategic choice by Tesla to delay. They note that Waymo still relies on more archaic, rules-based encoded systems rather than neural networks, and that Tesla's FSD is already operating at a level comparable or superior to what Waymo uses without a safety driver. The 20% reaction time improvement in 14.3 is cited as closing the last meaningful safety gap.

2. **Robotaxi Revenue as the True Stock Catalyst:** Herbert argues, drawing on Tesla's full stock history since IPO, that the only true catalyst for sustained stock price increases is earnings — specifically, repeated earnings beats over multiple quarters. A robotaxi city announcement or product demo will not move the stock meaningfully. The real inflection point will come when robotaxi revenue appears as a distinct line item on Tesla's balance sheet, analogous to how Apple's transition to a subscription model was only credited by Wall Street once the numbers were undeniable.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Germany Sales Hit Best-Ever March:** Tesla new car registrations in Germany quadrupled year-over-year in March 2026, representing the best March Tesla has ever recorded in Germany. The hosts frame this not merely as a recovery but as a record-breaking performance.

2. **Sales Rebounding Across Multiple Markets:** Beyond Germany, the hosts note that Tesla sales are up in South Korea and Japan, and are rebounding in China following the retooling disruptions of the prior year. Q1 2026 was acknowledged as soft overall, attributed to Q1 seasonal patterns and lingering effects from the end of IRA incentives.

3. **Model Y L as a Demand Contributor:** Herbert estimates the Model Y L (an apparently larger Model Y variant) could add approximately 10,000 to 20,000 incremental global sales, though he does not expect it to dramatically move overall delivery numbers. Brian speculates it may outperform Herbert's estimate, while acknowledging this is speculation without supporting data.

4. **FSD as a Demand Driver for Vehicle Sales:** Herbert identifies FSD wide release as a more significant demand driver than the Model Y L. He draws an analogy to Apple's transition from hardware to subscription revenue, suggesting Tesla is at a similar inflection point where FSD subscription uptake will eventually reshape how Wall Street values the company — but that this will only be reflected in stock price once it shows up in earnings results over multiple quarters.

## Market & Competition

1. **Intel Partnership on Terafab Is a Strategic Breakthrough:** Intel announced it will join Elon Musk's Terafab chip manufacturing project alongside SpaceX and Tesla. The hosts describe this as solving a key missing piece — access to advanced semiconductor manufacturing expertise. Intel is one of only a handful of companies in the world with knowledge of leading-edge chip fabrication processes (sub-5nm, approaching 2nm and below). Intel shares rose modestly on the announcement.

2. **Terafab Cost Estimate of $20 Billion:** Reports cited by the hosts suggest the Terafab project could cost approximately $20 billion with Intel's involvement — a figure the hosts describe as attractively low given the scale of the ambition, noting that China has already spent approximately half a trillion dollars just to reach 5nm fabrication capability.

3. **Samsung Already Committed; Intel Adds American Dimension:** Samsung had already agreed to build chip fab facilities in Taylor, Texas for Tesla, with plans for a second factory — both of which Tesla would absorb entirely. Intel's addition to the partnership brings the further advantage of being a domestic American company, which the hosts view as strategically important from a supply chain sovereignty standpoint.

4. **Intel Acquisition Floated as a Possibility:** The hosts reference a view from someone named "Joe" (not further identified) that Tesla or Elon Musk may ultimately acquire Intel outright. Brian notes that Elon himself had suggested buying Intel was an option, and that Intel likely joined the partnership partly to avoid that outcome.

5. **Waymo Falling Behind on Neural Network Transition:** The hosts assert that Waymo began with rules-based encoded systems rather than neural networks, and is only now beginning to transition. They credit Tesla as the clear leader in autonomous driving compute today, with the world's largest supercomputers dedicated primarily to FSD training, and a second system (Cortex 2) being developed for Optimus training.

6. **JP Morgan Bearish Calls Called Out:** The hosts mock JP Morgan's repeated sell ratings on Tesla, citing a calculation that if an investor had reduced their Tesla position by 1% every time JP Morgan issued a sell recommendation, their original $1 million investment would have gone to zero — while simply holding would have grown it to approximately $20 million. The hosts note that JP Morgan is itself one of Tesla's largest outside shareholders, which they find contradictory.

Notable quotes and data:
- FSD 14.3 delivers a **20% faster reaction time**, described by Tesla as the headline improvement.
- Germany Tesla registrations **quadrupled** in March 2026 — the **best March ever** for Tesla in Germany.
- Model Y L estimated to add **10,000–20,000** incremental global sales.
- Terafab estimated at **$20 billion** with Intel's involvement.
- China reportedly spent approximately **half a trillion dollars** to reach 5nm chip fabrication.
- David Moss tested FSD 14.3 for **over 10 hours**, with plans to extend to 15+ hours.
- **50+ testers** evaluated FSD 14.3 as of the recording date and deemed it ready for wide release.
- Herbert: *"The actual skyrocket of stock won't happen until you have not only earnings but you have earnings upon earnings growth."*
- Brian: *"When there is a separate line item for robo taxi revenue is when I expect Wall Street to go, 'Oh, dang. We forgot to front-run this.'"*
- Brian on Terafab skeptics: *"People said they couldn't make batteries... prior to Giga Nevada... they formed a partnership with Panasonic."*

2026-04-09.title: Will Tesla FSD 14.3 BOOST The Stock?
2026-04-09.body:
This video from the channel "jobhakdi," hosted by Jo Bhakdi, provides a rapid analysis of the newly released FSD version 14.3, examining what the update contains, why it matters for Tesla's robotaxi ambitions, and what it means for the stock. The core thesis is that while FSD 14.3 is a significant and foundational update — not a trivial one — it is not by itself the singular trigger for robotaxi deployment; rather, the decisive indicator remains whether unsupervised Cybercab production and scaling begins in April or May 2026. Jo Bhakdi frames the next six weeks as a critical window that will either validate or break the Tesla robotaxi investment thesis.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD 14.3 Released with Major Technical Improvements:** Tesla officially released FSD (Supervised) version 14.3, describing it as a broad and significant update. The most headline-grabbing improvement is a 20% faster reaction time, achieved by rewriting the AI compiler and runtime from the ground up using MLIR. Jo Bhakdi calls this "a very big deal," noting that faster reaction time across the board for an autonomous system responsible for human safety is critically important.

2. **Neural Network and Vision Encoder Upgrades:** The update includes reinforcement learning applied to the FSD neural network, enabling improvements across a wide variety of driving scenarios through a self-reinforcing learning loop across Tesla's entire fleet. The neural network vision encoder was also upgraded, specifically improving performance in rare and low-visibility conditions such as rain and sun glare, as well as strengthening 3D geometry understanding and expanding traffic sign recognition.

3. **Robotaxi-Focused Feature Set:** Several specific improvements in 14.3 point toward robotaxi readiness rather than supervised driver assistance. These include improved parking location pin prediction for complex environments like shopping mall lots, increased decisiveness in parking spot selection and maneuvering, enhanced response to emergency vehicles, improved handling of school buses, and better handling of small animals and unusual objects leaning into the vehicle path. Jo Bhakdi explicitly interprets this feature set as evidence of a strong internal focus on robotaxi use cases, noting that many of these features are trivial when a human driver is present but become critical when there is no one in the vehicle.

4. **Early Tester Impressions — Positive but Measured:** Early testers shared mixed-to-positive feedback. Tester Nick Cruz highlighted the faster reaction time as the standout improvement, noting the system finds parking spaces quicker, reacts at traffic lights faster, and performed "pretty much perfectly" in about 10 parking tests at a busy Costco lot. He also noted improved following distance with more space left to the car ahead. Tester Soya Merit noted more comfortable highway follow distance, quicker takeoff from stop signs, and reduced highway lane change hesitation, but said the version needs some smoothing out and characterized it as "setting the stage for something larger to come" with further reasoning capabilities expected in future updates. Jo Bhakdi summarizes these as important but not definitively game-changing reviews.

5. **14.3 as Foundation, Not Final Trigger:** Jo Bhakdi pushes back on the idea — attributed to Elon Musk's framing — that 14.3 is "the last missing piece" of autonomous transport. He believes Elon is "maybe hyping this a little bit too much." His view is that 14.3 is a very important foundational improvement that lays the groundwork for robotaxi, but that the real bottleneck for robotaxi rollout was never solely the software version — it is the convergence of many incremental improvements across software, hardware, and production readiness.

## Robotaxi

1. **Cybercab Production Start in April Is the Decisive Catalyst:** Jo Bhakdi states that his primary indicator for the robotaxi thesis has always been Cybercab production, specifically that mass production was targeted to start in April 2026. He frames this as the moment where Tesla must scale or risk looking like it wasted significant capex. The current robotaxi fleet tracker shows approximately 560 unsupervised vehicles, well short of his earlier prediction of 1,800, which he acknowledges is clearly not being met.

2. **Six-Week Window: April–May 2026 Is Make-or-Break:** Jo Bhakdi outlines a clear binary scenario for Tesla investors over the next six weeks (through end of May 2026). If unsupervised Cybercab scaling begins — even starting with just 10, then 20, then 40, then 80 units in an exponential ramp — he expects a major stock rally well beyond $500 per share. If unsupervised scaling does not begin by end of May, he predicts a deflation period for Tesla stock because the timeline becomes unknown and the thesis anchor breaks.

3. **Thesis Break Condition Defined:** Jo Bhakdi explicitly states that his thesis — that Cybercab is a reliable indicator of autonomous scaling — will break if unsupervised Cybercab deployment does not begin by end of May 2026. He allows for up to one month of delay from the April target (i.e., into May), but says beyond that, the investment case for near-term robotaxi becomes speculative and the stock will reprice downward. He notes this may be an unjust market reaction if deployment simply slips to June, but argues that is how the market will behave.

4. **Exponential Ramp Logic:** Jo Bhakdi argues that the starting number of unsupervised Cybercabs does not matter — what matters is that the ramp begins, because once started, growth will be exponential. He suggests that the starting point could be "multiple dozens" and will scale from there. The key investment signal is the inflection point of initiation, not the absolute fleet size at launch.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Model Y Mentioned as Secondary Robotaxi Vehicle:** Jo Bhakdi briefly references that unsupervised robotaxi operations could involve Model Y vehicles in addition to the Cybercab, though he characterizes the Cybercab as the primary focus and symbolic anchor of the robotaxi thesis.

## Market & Competition

1. **Macro Environment Improving for Tesla Stock:** Jo Bhakdi notes that macro conditions have improved, with what he describes as a reduction in geopolitical escalation risk — specifically referencing a reduction in Iran-related conflict risk from approximately 50% probability of bad escalation to less than 5% following a ceasefire. He argues that with this overhang reduced, markets are positioned to rally, and Tesla — having fallen more than other Magnificent 7 stocks — has more room to recover. However, he frames the question of whether Tesla reaches $600, $700, or $1,000 per share as entirely dependent on robotaxi becoming real.

2. **Waymo Referenced as Cautionary Benchmark:** Jo Bhakdi references Waymo twice as a negative example, noting that Tesla's robotaxi should not replicate Waymo's reported behavior of parking in the middle of streets and holding up traffic. He frames Tesla's improvements in parking decisiveness and reaction time as directly addressing the kinds of operational failures associated with Waymo's public deployments.

Notable quotes and data:
- FSD 14.3 delivers a **20% faster reaction time**, achieved by rewriting the AI compiler and runtime from scratch using MLIR.
- The AI compiler rewrite, neural network vision encoder upgrade, and reinforcement learning training are cited as the core technical pillars of the 14.3 release.
- Current unsupervised robotaxi tracker count: approximately **560 vehicles**.
- Jo Bhakdi's earlier prediction for this period was **1,800 unsupervised vehicles** — he explicitly acknowledges this target is not being met.
- Jo Bhakdi's thesis: if unsupervised Cybercab scaling does not begin by **end of May 2026**, the robotaxi investment thesis breaks and Tesla stock deflates.
- Stock price levels mentioned as potential targets if robotaxi scales: **$500, $600, $700, $1,000 per share**.
- Nick Cruz on 14.3: *"The biggest thing that stood out to me is the faster reaction time. 20% is very significant. It feels like it does things much quicker than before."*
- Soya Merit on 14.3: *"14.3 feels like it's setting the stage for something larger to come and that further reasoning capabilities will be added in future FSD updates."*
- Jo Bhakdi on Elon's framing: *"I think Elon is maybe hyping this a little bit too much, but it is a very important update."*

2026-04-10.title: Tesla: Delay or Big Month Ahead?
2026-04-10.body:
This video is a roundtable discussion hosted by "brighterwithherbert" featuring James from Invest Answers, Alexandra Merz, and Jeff Lutz, debating whether Tesla is experiencing meaningful delays or is on the cusp of major milestones. The panel covers FSD version 14.3, robotaxi deployment progress, Cybercab production, the speculative Tesla-SpaceX merger thesis, and broader market sentiment. The core argument is that while some milestones have slipped versus Q4 2025 guidance, the underlying signals — manufacturing ramp, city deployments, software rewrites — point toward imminent progress rather than structural delay.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD 14.3 Released — A Complete Rewrite, Not an Incremental Update:** FSD version 14.3 was released on Tuesday (approximately on time relative to Elon's end-of-week target), and the panel describes it as a ground-up rewrite of the AI compiler and runtime — not a minor update. The prior AI system was described as having been "dumbed down" because it couldn't fully leverage the Hardware 4 AI chip. Version 14.3 rebuilds the entire system to properly utilize that hardware, delivering a reported 20% improvement in reaction time speed. Early testers (estimated 50–100 people) are giving it strong reviews, describing it as smoother, faster, and more responsive.

2. **Version 15 Debate — 10x Parameter Model Deferred:** Elon posted that FSD version 15 — not 14.3 — will be the "large model" 10x parameter version that he says will "far exceed human levels of safety even in completely unsupervised and complex situations." This triggered community debate about whether robotaxi deployment is now delayed pending version 15. The panel pushes back, arguing that the small model used in version 14.3 has iterated faster than the large model, that version 15 has no specific date attached to it, and that version 14.3 is the platform on which unsupervised robotaxi expansion will proceed. Jeff Lutz notes that "banish" and other previously discussed features are objectively absent from 14.3, acknowledging valid concerns while maintaining that unsupervised FSD for personal vehicles remains the key near-term milestone.

3. **FSD Expansion to Europe — Netherlands Approval Pending:** The panel discusses a live poll showing 58% of viewers expect FSD approval in the Netherlands as of April 10, 2026 (the video's publish date). Alexandra Merz notes that some European users attempted to circumvent restrictions and had their FSD capability remotely deactivated by Tesla, illustrating Tesla's cautious regulatory approach. Full pin-to-pin FSD is described as available only in North America, Korea, and Australia at the time of recording. UK and German customers can purchase a full FSD package for approximately £8,000 / €8,000, but that package does not include address-to-address navigation.

4. **Version 14 Light for Hardware 3 Vehicles:** The panel notes (attributed to Cern) that the version 14.3 rewrite also enables a "version 14 light" to be made available for older Model 3 Hardware 3 vehicles, significantly expanding the addressable user base for the updated system.

## Robotaxi

1. **Austin and Bay Area Fleet — Safety Record and Expansion Signals:** The panel references NHTSA reports showing a strong safety record for Tesla's supervised robotaxi fleet operating in Austin and the Bay Area. Incident data cited: multiple fender-bender-only cases in December 2025–January 2026, declining to one low-speed case in the January 15–February 15 window. Jeff Lutz emphasizes that Tesla has been moving Model Y robotaxi vehicles equipped with Texas and California plates to five or six new U.S. cities, and that job requisitions for robotaxi operations staff continue to grow in quantity and variety across the United States — which he interprets as strong evidence the deployment plan remains on track.

2. **Unsupervised Expansion as the Key Near-Term Milestone:** The panel identifies the transition from supervised to unsupervised robotaxi operation — specifically in Austin and eventually the Bay Area — as the single most important near-term milestone, more important than earnings or volume deliveries. Jeff Lutz argues this will "go viral," change investor behavior, and potentially move the stock. The question he says should be asked at the earnings call is: what is Tesla's current understanding of when unsupervised FSD and unsupervised robotaxis will be released?

3. **Robotaxi Unit Economics — The Core Bull Case:** James presents a slide comparing Tesla's current car business economics to the robotaxi model. A sold car generates approximately $3,000 in one-time profit with an average holding period of about six years. A single Cybercab robotaxi is described as expected to generate $30,000–$50,000 in recurring annual profit. The cost to manufacture a Cybercab is cited at $15,000, though Jeff Lutz estimates the terminal production cost will likely settle between $18,000–$20,000 after at least a year of ramp. The panel describes this as a fundamental business model transformation from "shifting iron" to deploying income-generating robots.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Q1 2026 Deliveries — Inventory Spike Explained by Transit:** The panel addresses concern over Tesla's Q1 2026 delivery miss (described as within 1–2% of consensus for car deliveries, but with energy deliveries significantly below consensus). James highlights that China had its largest-ever export month in March 2026, with approximately 30,000 units, which he argues explains most or all of the apparent inventory spike. Jeff Lutz adds that Tesla's days of inventory moved from roughly 14–15 days in Q4 2025 to approximately 28–29 days in Q1 2026 — a pattern he says is similar to the same quarter transition in prior years and is not a demand signal, as 40–50% of that inventory is in transit.

2. **Model Q — Reported Development in China:** Reuters and Bloomberg reportedly confirmed that Tesla has contacted suppliers to build parts for a low-cost vehicle referred to as "Model Q," being developed in China. The panel is cautious about the sourcing (unnamed, unsourced), but Jeff Lutz notes that if development is genuinely underway in China, Tesla could ship the vehicle as early as next year (2027) given China's rapid product development cadence. He suggests the Model Q will likely reuse Cybercab parts to reduce complexity.

3. **BEV Sales Uptick in Europe — Oil Price Correlation:** James notes an early data signal showing a significant uptick in battery electric vehicle sales in Europe in March 2026. He also presents a chart showing an inverse correlation between oil prices and Tesla's stock price — as oil prices decline, Tesla's stock historically rises — framing lower oil as a potential tailwind for EV demand.

## Humanoid Bots
