Their view is that AI5 has not been dropped from vehicles — it simply isn't critical to achieving unsupervised FSD on AI4, and will be incorporated into cars when AI4 goes out of production and AI5 becomes sufficiently available and cost-effective.

5. **FSD Approved in the Netherlands, Europe Expansion:** The hosts note that FSD has received regulatory approval in the Netherlands and is expected to launch across Europe during summer 2026. They characterize the EU regulatory path as a "patchwork quilt" of approvals, with the Netherlands approval serving as the first domino. Implications for a robotaxi strategy in Europe are acknowledged but not fully answered.

6. **Distributed Compute via Superchargers/Fleet:** The hosts discuss a community question about using Tesla vehicles and Superchargers as a distributed inference network. Based on a conversation with a chip designer, the host flags two key obstacles: data security concerns (customers paying for compute may object to data being distributed across a consumer vehicle fleet) and latency issues from vehicles being geographically dispersed and on variable Wi-Fi connections. Their conclusion is this is a longer-term possibility, not near-term.

## Robotaxi
1. **Robotaxi Geographic Expansion — Current Status:** The hosts note active robotaxi activity in several new areas beyond Austin, including Florida, Nevada, and additional locations in Texas. A Cybercab was reportedly spotted in Chicago by Rob Mau on the day of recording. The hosts expect Tesla to discuss expansion into new markets on the earnings call, likely reiterating last year's goal of reaching half the U.S. population.

2. **Revenue Expectations Remain Modest:** The hosts agree that robotaxi revenue in 2026 will be lackluster. They note that meaningful FSD recurring revenue would require unsupervised approval — which they do not expect this year — making near-term robotaxi revenue minor. They also flag NHTSA safety data filings as a topic they hope the earnings call will address, since safety validation may be the primary bottleneck to scaling the fleet.

3. **Robotaxi Expansion Timeline — Skepticism on Pace:** Both hosts maintain skepticism about rapid rollout, with the host noting he was present at the shareholder meeting when ambitious end-of-year goals were announced and immediately doubted the timeline. They expect the earnings call guidance to largely reiterate last year's targets rather than announce major acceleration.

## Energy
1. **Solar Strategy — Waiting on Tesla's Own Solar Fab:** In response to a question about stalled residential solar deployments and whether Tesla will pivot to utility-scale solar or battery farms, the host suggests Tesla is waiting for its own solar fabrication facility to reach higher throughput before aggressively scaling. He argues Tesla has unique advantages in consuming its own solar supply across parking lots, industrial rooftops, and Supercharger canopies, but that the solar fab needs to come online at scale first. The guest notes this is not Tesla's primary current focus and unlikely to be a major earnings call topic.

## Electric Vehicles
1. **New Vehicle — "Better Than a Minivan":** The hosts briefly address Elon Musk's posts on X teasing a new vehicle described as better than a minivan, speculated to potentially be a "Model Y L" or similar. Both expect Tesla to decline to comment during the earnings call, stating such a reveal warrants its own dedicated event.

Notable quotes and data:
- Optimus Gen 3 reveal expected: Q2 or Q3 2026 (hosts' best guess)
- Optimus production start: likely not before midyear 2026; SNX factory tooling changeover possibly beginning around May 12th
- Optimus year-end 2026 production: possibly fewer than 1,000 total units; hosts explicitly say "it might not even end at a thousand"
- Early Optimus units will run on AI4 chip, not AI5
- FSD v14.3 is out to a number of users and remains supervised
- FSD approved in the Netherlands; expected Europe-wide launch summer 2026
- Robot half-marathon: 400+ entries in 2026 (up from ~100 in 2025); winning robot beat human record by ~57 minutes
- Cybercab spotted in Chicago (photo shared by Rob Mau)
- Robotaxi activity confirmed in Florida, Nevada, and multiple Texas locations
- Host on Elon's FSD promises: "He said definitely by the end of next year, since 2012, 14"

2026-04-22.title: Tesla Q1 Earnings CALL! GET IN HERE!
2026-04-22.body:
This video is a live stream covering Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call, hosted by "investingagainstthegrain" with a panel of analysts and commentators including James (Invest Answers), Larry Goldberg, Nick Gibbs, Jeff Lutz, Alexandra Merz, and Cern Basher. The panel analyzes the earnings deck as it drops, live-streams the official Tesla earnings call featuring Elon Musk and CFO Vaibhav Taneja, and then conducts a post-call discussion. The core thesis across the panel is that Tesla is at a major inflection point driven by the convergence of Cybercab production launch, robotaxi expansion, Optimus development, and FSD adoption growth — though the panel is critical of Tesla's communication style on the call itself.

## Financials

1. **Free Cash Flow Dramatically Beats Expectations:** Tesla reported Q1 2026 free cash flow of just over $1.4 billion positive, against Wall Street consensus estimates of approximately negative $1.9 billion — a swing of roughly $3.5 billion. The panel attributed this primarily to stronger-than-expected gross margins driven by lower vehicle material costs and growth in high-margin services revenue (FSD). Cash on hand increased to $44.7 billion in the quarter.

2. **Gross Margin Returns to Multi-Year Highs:** GAAP gross margin came in at 21.1%, with auto gross margin excluding credits at 19.2% (up sequentially from 17.9%). The panel noted this is the highest gross margin level since approximately Q4 2022. Auto gross profit per vehicle delivered, excluding credits and leases, exceeded $8,000. One-time benefits included approximately $230 million from warranty true-ups and some tariff relief, though no benefit from the recent Supreme Court IPA tariff ruling was recognized due to ongoing uncertainty.

3. **Capex Guidance Raised Sharply to $25 Billion for 2026:** CFO Vaibhav Taneja disclosed that Tesla now expects over $25 billion in capital expenditures for full-year 2026, up $5 billion from prior guidance of $20 billion. In Q1, Tesla spent approximately $2.5 billion in capex (or roughly $4.5 billion including the ~$2 billion equity investment in SpaceX/XAI made in January). Management explicitly stated that free cash flow will be negative for the remainder of 2026, describing this as the right strategy for long-term positioning. The panel noted six factories are currently going into or already in operation.

4. **Services Revenue at All-Time Record for Q1:** Services and other revenue reached $3.745 billion, up approximately 10% sequentially from Q3's $3.475 billion and down slightly from Q4, representing a 51% increase year-over-year. The panel noted this is primarily driven by FSD subscriptions and supercharging, and that this was an all-time Q1 record for the segment. Energy generation and storage revenue fell from approximately $3.8 billion to $2.4 billion quarter-over-quarter, with management confirming the business is inherently lumpy tied to customer deployment timelines.

5. **Net Income Impacted by Bitcoin and FX:** Net income was impacted by mark-to-market charges on Bitcoin holdings, which depreciated 22% compared to the prior quarter, as well as unfavorable FX impacts from intercompany transactions. Net profit margin was approximately 6.5%.

6. **CEO Compensation Expense Hits P&L:** Operating expenses increased sequentially due to a full quarter of stock-based compensation for the 2025 CEO compensation plan, for which one milestone is still deemed probable. The weighted average diluted share count remained essentially flat at approximately 3.538–3.539 billion shares.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Demand Rebounds in Key Markets:** CFO Taneja reported demand resurgence across multiple regions. Giga Berlin reached a record output of over 61,000 units in Q1 2026. France and Germany showed over 150% quarter-over-quarter growth in deliveries. South Korea and Japan also showed growth. The US saw slight quarter-over-quarter delivery growth. Tesla ended Q1 with its highest Q1 order backlog in over two years. The recent uptick in gas prices provided a tailwind, though management noted improvement began before gas prices rose.

2. **Battery Cell Availability Remains a Production Constraint:** Management explicitly flagged battery pack capacity as the biggest limiter on vehicle production growth. Remediation efforts underway include ramping the Model Y in-house 4680 battery pack in Berlin, adding capacity at the Reno facility (retooling lines after nearly 10 years), and ramping in-house LFP module production in China. Tesla also began ramping LFP production for Megapacks.

3. **Model 3 Affordability Highlighted:** CFO Taneja noted that when Model 3 launched with a promised $35,000 starting price, that equates to approximately $48,000 in today's dollars, while the current starting price of Model 3 is below that figure with a substantially more capable product.

4. **Vehicle Sales Strategy Shift — FSD as the Product:** Management stated Tesla has evolved its sales strategy to position FSD as the primary product and the vehicle as merely the delivery mechanism.

5. **Hardware 3 Cannot Achieve Unsupervised FSD:** Elon Musk confirmed that Hardware 3 vehicles lack the capability to run unsupervised FSD, citing that Hardware 3 has only 1/8 the memory bandwidth of Hardware 4, which is a critical bottleneck for AI inference. Tesla is offering discounted trade-ins toward Hardware 4 vehicles and plans to offer in-car hardware upgrades (requiring replacement of both the computer and cameras). To do this efficiently, Tesla plans to establish micro-factories or small upgrade centers in major metropolitan areas. A distilled version of V14 software for Hardware 3 is expected to be released by end of June, enabling park-to-drive and equivalent features to V14 on Hardware 4.

6. **Tesla Roadster Debut Possible in About a Month:** Elon Musk mentioned that a Tesla Roadster debut could happen in approximately a month, contingent on testing and validation. He described it as potentially "one of the most spectacular demos ever" but noted it won't be a significant revenue driver. He also confirmed that long-term, the only manually-driven Tesla will be the new Roadster — all other models are intended to be autonomous.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD Version 14.3 Is a Major Architectural Update — Last Piece of the Puzzle:** Elon Musk confirmed that FSD V14.3 represents a major architectural update and is essentially the last piece needed to enable unsupervised FSD. However, he clarified that further software improvements (including V15, a complete software architecture overhaul) are known and in the pipeline, and Tesla will not go to very large-scale unsupervised FSD deployment until those improvements are validated and released, because they could materially improve safety.

2. **FSD Version 15 — Complete Software Overhaul Planned:** Elon Musk described V15 as a "complete overhaul of the software architecture" that will run on AI4 hardware. He stated it is expected by the end of 2026, or certainly by early 2027. V15 is intended to further elevate safety beyond already-above-human levels. The robotaxi fleet in Austin, Dallas, and Houston is running on V14.3 variants.

3. **FSD Subscriptions Hit Nearly 1.3 Million Paid Customers Globally:** CFO Taneja reported nearly 1.3 million paid FSD customers globally as of Q1. FSD subscriptions grew 180,000 in the quarter (the fastest sequential quarterly growth ever for FSD). Approximately 14% of all Tesla vehicles ever delivered now have an active FSD subscription. The incremental take rate for Q1 was over 50% (though the panel noted this is skewed by the removal of outright purchase option driving people to subscribe). FSD miles driven reached approximately 9.7 billion, on track to cross 10 billion by approximately mid-May.

4. **FSD Approved in Netherlands; EU-Wide Review Expected in Q2:** Tesla received FSD supervised approval in the Netherlands. The broader EU review is expected in May (submitted to Brussels), potentially enabling FSD across Europe by Q2. China approval is also in progress, with hopes for broader approval by Q3 2026. Management noted Europe data was incorporated into the same underlying FSD architecture used in the US.

5. **AI4 Chip Sufficient for Unsupervised FSD; AI5 Redirected:** Elon Musk confirmed that AI4 hardware is expected to achieve unsupervised FSD at safety levels far exceeding human drivers, meaning AI5 is not immediately needed in vehicles. AI5 will go into Optimus and data centers (Cortex). An AI4 upgrade (dubbed "AI4.1" or "AI4 plus") is planned, upgrading RAM from 16GB to 32GB per SoC (64GB total), with approximately 10% improvements in compute and memory bandwidth. This upgrade depends on Samsung completing modifications and is expected to go into production around mid-2027. AI6 design is underway and Dojo 3 concepts are being discussed.

6. **AI5 Chip Tape-Out Completed Early:** The AI5 chip tape-out was completed ahead of schedule, achieved through the team working every weekend for six months straight including all holidays. Elon Musk personally participated. No major design mistakes were encountered.

7. **Unsupervised FSD to Customer Cars — Likely Q4 2026:** Elon Musk estimated, with caveats, that unsupervised FSD will be made available to customer-owned vehicles approximately in Q4 2026, rolled out gradually by geography as each area is confirmed safe.

8. **Hardware 3 Upgrade Path Detailed:** For Hardware 3 owners with purchased FSD, Tesla is offering a discounted trade-in toward a Hardware 4 vehicle or an in-car upgrade (computer + camera replacement). Micro-factory upgrade centers are being planned for major metro areas to execute this efficiently at scale.

9. **Cortex 1 Operational; Cortex 2 Online and Running Training Workloads:** Cortex 1 is in production with over 100,000 H100-equivalent GPUs. Cortex 2 has started running training workloads (an early ramp phase). A picture of Cortex 2 was referenced as being posted publicly.

## Robotaxi

1. **Cybercab Production Has Started:** During the live stream, Jeff Lutz reported breaking news that Tesla's X account confirmed Cybercab production has officially started, posted approximately 10 minutes before the announcement. The earnings deck described Cybercab as being in "pilot production" at time of publication. Elon Musk confirmed on the call that production has "just started." He cautioned that initial production will be very slow, following a typical S-curve for any new product with an entirely new supply chain, expected to ramp exponentially toward year-end and into 2027.

2. **Cybercab, Tesla Semi, and Megapack 3 All On Track for Volume Production in 2026:** The earnings deck explicitly states all three are on schedule for volume production in 2026. The panel noted this is one of the most significant headlines from the deck.

3. **Robotaxi Expanding to Dallas and Houston — Unsupervised from Day One:** Tesla expanded robotaxi operations to Dallas and Houston, launching unsupervised (no safety driver) from the outset, which the panel noted is unprecedented — other companies (notably Waymo) spent two or more years in supervised mode in new cities. The earnings deck listed seven cities in various stages from "ramping unsupervised" to "preparations underway."

4. **Target: Approximately a Dozen States by End of 2026:** Elon Musk stated Tesla hopes to have unsupervised FSD or robotaxi operating in approximately a dozen or more states by end of 2026. He emphasized a very cautious approach — zero incidents and zero injuries to date with the unsupervised expansion. He confirmed robotaxi revenue will not be "super material" in 2026 but expects it to be material and possibly significant in 2027.

5. **Primary Bottleneck Is Operational, Not Safety:** Elon Musk and Ashok Elluswami detailed that the primary issues slowing robotaxi scale-up are operational edge cases, not direct safety incidents: cars getting "scared" and refusing to cross railroads or proceed at stuck lights; cars caught in recursive infinite loops (e.g., attempting a turn into a construction zone repeatedly); and a notable incident where a group of Tesla robotaxis were stuck in a left-turn lane in Austin because a Waymo had crashed into a bus blocking the road.

6. **Cybercab to Replace Model Y Fleet Over Time:** The earnings deck explicitly states that once in production, Cybercab will begin replacing the existing Model Y fleet and is expected to become the largest volume vehicle in Tesla's fleet over time. Elon Musk noted that 90% of miles driven are with one or two people, making the two-person Cybercab the logical primary vehicle.

7. **Fleet Ramp Projections (Analyst Panel Estimates):** Jeff Lutz estimated hundreds of Cybercabs per month in April, ramping to approximately 1,000 per month by end of June, with the expectation that by end of Q3 Tesla could produce the equivalent of the entire Waymo fleet in one month, and within six months could produce the Waymo fleet's equivalent in one week. Nick Gibbs suggested Tesla could have more robotaxis deployed than Waymo's entire fleet by end of May or June 2026 due to the forcing function of Cybercab production.

8. **Robotaxi Revenue in Services Line:** CFO Taneja confirmed robotaxi revenue is included in the Services and Other segment. Tesla is making deliberate infrastructure investments to support robotaxi scaling. The fleet grew quarter-over-quarter in Q1.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus V3 Reveal Expected Around Mid-2026:** Elon Musk stated the V3 Optimus design is "almost ready to demonstrate" with some aesthetic finishing touches remaining. He expects to be able to show it off approximately mid-year 2026. However, Tesla is deliberately delaying the reveal to avoid competitors doing frame-by-frame analysis and copying the design — and intends to show it closer to the point of production.

2. **Optimus Production Start at Fremont — Late July/August 2026:** Elon Musk stated Optimus starter production at Fremont is assumed to be somewhere around late July to August 2026. The final Model S/X production will end in early May, after which the production line will be fully dismantled. Elon explained the full process: dismantling the old line starting from sub-components up to final assembly (over several months), then installing new cabling, machines, and testing for the Optimus line. He stated completing this transition in approximately four months would be "an insanely fast speed" unprecedented by any company on Earth.

3. **Optimus First Large-Scale Factory Preparations Beginning in Q2 2026:** The earnings deck states preparations for Tesla's first large-scale Optimus factory will begin shortly in Q2 2026 — earlier than the previously expected Q3 start. A second Optimus factory is being constructed at Giga Texas, expected to start production around summer 2027.

4. **Optimus Production Rate for 2026 Cannot Be Predicted:** Elon Musk explicitly stated it is "impossible to predict" the Optimus production rate for 2026 given the entirely new product, entirely new production line, and approximately 10,000 unique components that all must go right. He stated it "will move as fast as the least lucky, slowest, dumbest part in the entire 10,000." Initial skills will start simple (factory tasks) and build up from there.

5. **Optimus Useful Outside Tesla Expected Starting 2027:** Elon Musk stated Tesla expects to be able to make Optimus useful outside of Tesla (i.e., for external customers) sometime in 2027. He reiterated his conviction that Optimus will be "probably the biggest product ever," not just Tesla's biggest product.

6. **Optimus Intelligence Architecture — Local + Grok Orchestration:** Elon Musk described the planned intelligence architecture for Optimus: sufficient local on-board AI to continue functioning even without cellular or Wi-Fi connectivity (analogous to how FSD works offline in cars). Grok is intended as the orchestration AI (similar to a manager) and for voice interaction. He estimated Optimus could work for several hours without requiring management oversight from a large AI model.

## Energy

1. **Q1 Energy Storage Deployments Decline Significantly:** Tesla deployed 6.8 gigawatt hours of energy storage in Q1 2026, a 38% sequential decline. Management attributed this to the inherently lumpy nature of the business tied to customer deployment timelines. Despite the decline, Tesla still expects full-year 2026 energy storage deployments to exceed 2025 levels. Energy gross margins hit a record 39.5%, partly due to one-time benefits of over $250 million from recognition of tariffs paid in prior quarters. On a normalized basis, management expects energy margin compression going forward due to increasing competition and tariff impacts (most battery cells are sourced from China).

2. **Megapack 3 Factory in Houston On Track:** Tesla's new Megapack factory outside Houston (referred to as "Megafactory") is on track to begin production later in 2026. Starter production for the new Megapack factory is on track per the earnings deck.

3. **Residential Solar in Correction; New Products Introduced:** Management noted the US residential solar market is going through a correction following the loss of the homeowner tax credit. Tesla introduced a solar lease product to capture the tax credit itself and offer competitive pricing. Tesla also debuted its own solar panel with superior performance and aesthetics, plus its own mounting system for a fully integrated home energy ecosystem. Strong demand is expected to resume in the second half of 2026.

## Market & Competition

1. **Goldman Sachs Safety Report Validates Tesla Robotaxi Advantage:** The panel referenced a Goldman Sachs safety report comparing Tesla and Waymo incident data using NHTSA filings, which the panel noted is the first time Goldman Sachs has dug into incident data between the two companies. The report concluded that Tesla's robotaxi has a "massive advantage in safety" and that the advantage becomes more obvious at scale. Goldman called Tesla a "true leader in autonomous driving AI." The panel noted no Tesla robotaxi incidents since January 15, 2026.

2. **Waymo Comparison on Fleet and Timeline:** The panel noted Waymo spent over two years in supervised mode in both Scottsdale/Phoenix and the Bay Area before going unsupervised. Jeff Lutz predicted Tesla could produce the equivalent of Waymo's entire fleet in one month by end of Q3 2026, and in one week within six months after that.

3. **Terafab Structure and Intel Partnership Disclosed:** Tesla disclosed that its research semiconductor fab on the Giga Texas campus will be approximately a $3 billion initiative capable of producing a few thousand wafers per month, intended for R&D and testing new chip manufacturing physics. Intel will partner on the core manufacturing technology using Intel's 14A process node. SpaceX will handle the initial phase of the larger-scale Terafab. The research fab will uniquely integrate lithography mask creation, logic, memory, and packaging under one roof for rapid R&D iteration. The panel noted the complexity of the Tesla/SpaceX joint governance structure as a friction point.

4. **Tesla's $2 Billion SpaceX/XAI Equity Investment:** Tesla recorded a $2 billion equity investment in SpaceX (specifically XAI) during Q1, which was announced on approximately January 28, 2026. The panel debated whether this was included in the original $20 billion capex forecast.

5. **Tariffs Creating Cost Pressure Across Businesses:** CFO Taneja noted that both tariffs and sustained high interest rates continue to add to automotive costs. Interest rate subvention costs are recognized upfront. In the energy business, tariffs can have outsized impacts since most battery cells are sourced from China. Tesla is actively regionalizing and vertically integrating critical supply chains in response to trade and geopolitical uncertainty.

Notable quotes and data:
- Free cash flow: +$1.4 billion vs. consensus estimate of approximately -$1.9 billion
- GAAP gross margin: 21.1%; Auto gross margin ex-credits: 19.2% (highest since ~2022)
- Auto gross profit per vehicle ex-credits and leases: over $8,000
- Cash on hand: $44.7 billion
- FSD paid customers globally: nearly 1.3 million
- FSD subscription growth Q1: +180,000 (fastest sequential growth ever)
- FSD miles driven: ~9.7 billion, approaching 10 billion by ~mid-May
- FSD subscriptions as % of all vehicles ever delivered: ~14%
- Incremental FSD take rate for Q1: over 50%
- Services revenue year-over-year growth: +51%
- Energy storage deployed Q1: 6.8 gigawatt hours (-38% sequentially)
- Energy gross margin: 39.5% (record, includes ~$250M one-time tariff benefit)
- Giga Berlin Q1 output: record 61,000+ units
- Full-year 2026 capex guidance: over $25 billion (up from $20 billion)
- Cortex 1: operational, 100,000+ H100-equivalent GPUs
- Terafab research lab: ~$3 billion initiative, few thousand wafers/month capacity
- AI4.1 upgrade: 16GB → 32GB RAM per SoC (64GB total), ~10% compute improvement, mid-2027 production (pending Samsung)
- Optimus production start target: late July/August 2026 at Fremont
- Second Optimus factory at Giga Texas: production start ~summer 2027
- Optimus useful outside Tesla: expected starting 2027
- Robotaxi target: approximately a dozen or more US states by end of 2026
- Hardware 3 memory bandwidth: 1/8 that of Hardware 4
- V15 FSD: expected by end of 2026 or early 2027; complete architecture overhaul; runs on AI4
- Elon Musk on Cybercab production: "We've just started production of Cybercab and we'll begin production of our semi-truck soon"
- Elon Musk on Optimus: "I think Optimus will be our biggest product, not just Tesla's biggest product ever, but probably the biggest product ever"
- Elon Musk on robotaxi safety: "We don't want to have a single accident or injury with the expansion of robo taxi and we have, to the credit of the team, not had a single one to date"
- Elon Musk on scale: Tesla hopes for unsupervised FSD/robotaxi in "a dozen or so states by end of this year"
- Elon Musk on FSD to customer cars: "Probably in the fourth quarter" (Q4 2026)
- France and Germany deliveries: over 150% quarter-over-quarter growth in Q1 2026
- Tesla's Q1 order backlog: highest Q1 backlog in over two years
- Jeff Lutz fleet ramp estimate: hundreds/month in April → ~1,000/month by end of June → Waymo-fleet-equivalent production per month by end of Q3

2026-04-22.title: How I PLAYED Tesla Earnings (Stock Options)
2026-04-22.body:
This video, published on Tesla earnings day (April 22, 2026) by Jo Bhakdi, lays out a pre-earnings analytical framework and options trading strategy for Tesla. Rather than focusing on granular EPS or delivery estimates, Jo Bhakdi argues that robotaxi trajectory and guidance are far more material to Tesla's valuation than near-term earnings beats or misses. He then explains why he is selling short puts into earnings, using Polymarket data and options pricing to argue that downside risk is already largely priced in.

## Financials
1. **Consensus EPS estimates and net income range:** The analyst consensus heading into earnings is 33 cents adjusted EPS (based on 20 analysts), with a broader Refinitiv/FactSet range of 36–37 cents. In absolute dollar terms, Jo Bhakdi translates this to a low-end estimate of approximately $1 billion in net profit for the quarter and a high-end estimate of approximately $1.3 billion. He notes that a miss of roughly 10% would represent a swing of approximately 4 cents per share — a number he argues is dwarfed in significance by robotaxi trajectory.

2. **Why EPS misses matter less than robotaxi math:** Jo Bhakdi presents a simplified framework to contextualize the earnings numbers relative to robotaxi economics. Assuming $60,000 in margin per robotaxi per year, a $1 billion quarterly net income figure is equivalent to the annualized earnings contribution of approximately 66,000 robotaxis. A 10% earnings miss — roughly $100 million — would be fully offset by just 1,600 robotaxis on a quarterly basis, or approximately 6,000 on an annualized basis. He uses this to argue that any upward revision to robotaxi fleet guidance would easily override even a meaningful EPS miss.

3. **Expectations for what Tesla will say on the call:** Jo Bhakdi anticipates Tesla will offer cautious, non-committal language on the robotaxi rollout — affirming that expansion into Dallas and Houston is underway, citing regulatory progress in the Netherlands as an important unlock for broader European deployment, and emphasizing a safety-first approach. He expects no concrete fleet size targets or timelines to be disclosed, consistent with Tesla's pattern over the prior four earnings calls.

## Robotaxi
1. **Robotaxi guidance as the dominant stock catalyst:** Jo Bhakdi argues that the market's reaction to earnings will be driven primarily by any changes in robotaxi deployment guidance rather than by the headline EPS number. He outlines a spectrum of hypothetical fleet ramp scenarios — from 6,000 to 12,000 to 40,000 to 200,000 vehicles — and asserts that any upward revision in these numbers would be a far more powerful stock catalyst than a beat on quarterly income. He characterizes the current rollout as slow but continuous, with recent "step changes" on unsupervised operations occurring on a low base.

2. **Known rollout milestones heading into earnings:** As of the video date, Jo Bhakdi references that unsupervised robotaxi operations have been added in Dallas and Houston, and that Tesla has received regulatory approval in the Netherlands, which he frames as a key domino for unlocking broader European deployment. He acknowledges the Cybercab is scaling but emphasizes the base remains small.

## Market & Competition
1. **Pre-earnings stock behavior and Polymarket signal:** Jo Bhakdi highlights that Tesla's stock underperformed its expected beta (approximately 2x the NASDAQ) in the day leading up to earnings, falling roughly $10 from around $400 on April 21, 2026, while the NASDAQ itself was not weak. He correlates this with a sharp drop on Polymarket's "Will Tesla beat quarterly earnings?" contract, which fell from 33% probability to approximately 18–20% in the same window. He interprets this as evidence of a likely information leak and treats the low beat-probability reading as a bullish setup for options positioning.

2. **Options strategy — short puts into earnings:** Based on his analysis, Jo Bhakdi describes selling short puts with a Friday expiration at strikes of 390, 385, 380, or as conservatively as 375, noting that the 375 strike was offering approximately $3–4 in premium, implying a breakeven near $371. He reasons that with only ~18% probability of a beat priced in, the market has already discounted a significant portion of any potential downside move. His base case is a flat-to-slightly-positive stock reaction (±2% or less), with tail risk skewed to the upside rather than the downside. He explicitly cautions beginners against excessive position sizing and emphasizes survivability if the stock were to fall to $350.

Notable quotes and data:
- Consensus EPS: 33 cents adjusted (20-analyst consensus); broader range 36–37 cents
- Implied net income range: ~$1 billion (low end) to ~$1.3 billion (high end) for the quarter
- Assumed robotaxi margin: $60,000 per vehicle per year
- Robotaxis needed to generate $1 billion/quarter in net income: ~66,000 (annualized)
- A 10% earnings miss (~$100M quarterly) offset by just ~1,600 robotaxis per quarter, or ~6,000 annualized
- Polymarket beat probability: dropped from ~33% to ~18–20% on April 21, 2026
- Tesla stock fell ~$10 (from ~$400) on April 21 while NASDAQ was relatively stable
- Tesla trading at roughly half its beta-implied move (~2.2% expected, actual ~half that) on earnings day
- Options implied move: approximately $10 built into the at-the-money straddle (~$390 strike)
- Short put strikes discussed: 390, 385, 380, 375 — 375 strike yielding approximately $3–4 premium, breakeven ~$371
- "Any kind of change in the outlook for robo taxi will massively override to the downside or upside that miss number."
- "Get the odds on your side. No one knows the future, but we can predict the future in a way that puts the odds on our sides."

2026-04-22.title: Cadillac Escalade IQ Interior Review: Does the Quality Match the Price?
2026-04-22.body:
This video from Munro Live features an interior review of the Cadillac Escalade IQ electric SUV, presented by a self-described Cadillac enthusiast who attempts to apply a critical eye despite her personal affinity for the brand. The core thesis is that while the Escalade IQ is a genuinely original electric vehicle (not a rebadged existing model) and largely delivers on luxury expectations for its $150,000 price point, there are several notable quality and design shortfalls — particularly in stitching consistency, second-row seat materials and functionality, and some finish details — that fall short of what a buyer should expect at this price.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Escalade IQ as a Unique Electric Platform:** The reviewer emphasizes that unlike the original Escalade, which was a rebadged Yukon, the Escalade IQ is a purpose-built electric vehicle unique to itself. She views this as a meaningful distinction and credits Cadillac for developing an original platform rather than converting an existing one.

2. **Price Point and Value Assessment:** The Cadillac Escalade IQ is priced at $150,000. The reviewer acknowledges that a significant portion of that cost is in the drivetrain and technology, and estimates that a comparable-sized EV without luxury features might cost $80,000–$90,000. She concludes that the overall package largely justifies the cost, but with specific reservations.

3. **Interior Materials — Strengths:** The upper door roll features real cut-and-sew stitching on a thin foam-backed material, which the reviewer considers appropriate for the price. The lower instrument panel is fully wrapped in what she believes is a silicone-based artificial leather (not PVC or PUR), a material Cadillac has reportedly been investing in. She notes that using artificial leather allows for a single wide continuous sheet — something difficult to achieve with natural leather hides at this vehicle's scale. Pillar trim and overhead lining use artificial suede.

4. **Interior Materials — Weaknesses and Quality Issues:** The reviewer identifies several quality shortfalls inconsistent with the $150,000 price tag. Stitching on the top roll and overhead lining is uneven and wavy in places, with frayed threads visible and stitching pulling away at corners. A door panel has an awkward formation where it hugs the instrument panel, breaking the visual line. The faux wood grain trim throughout uses a high-gloss finish, which the reviewer dislikes — she prefers open-pore texture that mimics real wood. The cargo area shows raw-cut hardboard edges beneath carpet, which she considers a cheap finish detail.

5. **Second Row Seat Criticisms:** The reviewer is critical of the second-row seats on multiple fronts. The plastic side shields on the second-row seats have sharp parting lines, a glossy low-quality texture, and are described as indistinguishable from what one might find in a $30,000 vehicle — she suspects the CAD geometry was borrowed from another vehicle. Despite the front seats offering heated, cooled, and massage functionality, the second-row seats are manually adjustable, which she argues is unacceptable at this price point, noting that power second-row seats have been implemented in vehicles costing less than half as much.

6. **Integrated Seatback Screens — Skepticism:** The Escalade IQ includes integrated video screens in the front seatbacks for second-row passengers. The reviewer dislikes this feature for several reasons: the screens are bespoke to the vehicle, making them expensive to replace (she estimates five times the cost of a consumer product like an iPad); they cannot be updated as display technology improves over the vehicle's lifespan; and their exposed position makes them vulnerable to damage, especially from children. She contrasts this with recessed seatback screen designs she has worked on previously, which trade screen size for better protection.

7. **Third Row and Seat Controls:** The third-row seats are fully powered and can be folded and raised from rear cargo area controls. However, the second-row seats — despite having a power release — cannot be raised from the rear controls, only folded forward. The reviewer flags this as an inconsistency in the seat control logic.

8. **Design Details — Positives:** The reviewer highlights several design choices she appreciates. Chrome accents are used sparingly and with a textured finish that gives a jewelry-like quality at no additional manufacturing cost (the texture is cut directly into the injection mold tool). Door pocket edges use a generous radius rather than sharp parting lines typical of low-cost vehicles. The glass panoramic roof, while fixed (non-opening, non-shaded), is tinted. The historical Cadillac crest with marletes (heraldic ducks) is preserved on the instrument panel, even though simplified crest versions without marletes are used on all other badges throughout the vehicle.

## Market & Competition

1. **Cadillac's Historical Identity vs. Present Execution:** The reviewer contextualizes her criticism within Cadillac's heritage as a brand that was once "the standard of the world," historically first with its own engines and technology. She argues that the Escalade IQ represents a meaningful return to originality for the Escalade nameplate as an EV, but that some execution details undermine the premium positioning the brand commands.

Notable quotes and data:
- Price of Cadillac Escalade IQ: **$150,000**
- Estimated baseline EV cost without luxury features at this size: **$80,000–$90,000**
- Reviewer's estimate of bespoke seatback screen cost vs. consumer equivalent: **~5x the cost of an iPad** (estimated $500–$1,000 for a consumer tablet)
- Interior artificial leather described as likely **silicone-based**, not PVC or PUR
- Second-row seat side shields characterized as equivalent in quality to a **$30,000 vehicle**
- Third-row seats are **fully powered**; second-row seats are **manual** (with power release only)
- Glass roof is **fixed, tinted, non-opening, with no sunshade**
- The Cadillac crest **marletes** appear only on the instrument panel badge, not on other exterior or interior badges
- *"For $150,000 vehicle, I don't know if that's enough. I might be the only person in the world who notices, but it bugs me."* — on the second-row seat side shields
- *"You are never replacing the screen. And since it is bespoke and unique to the vehicle, the cost of these screens are easily five times the cost of a consumer product like an iPad."*

2026-04-22.title: Cadillac Escalade IQ Quality
2026-04-22.body:
This video from Munro Live features a brief quality inspection of the Cadillac Escalade IQ's interior, focusing on stitching and trim execution. The analyst examines frayed threads and stitching alignment issues around curved surfaces, raising concerns about the manufacturing quality of the vehicle's interior. No Tesla-specific content is covered in this transcript excerpt.

## Market & Competition
1. **Cadillac Escalade IQ interior stitching quality concerns:** The reviewer identifies frayed threads along interior stitching on the Cadillac Escalade IQ, noting that the thread quality used in the sewing process appears to be a contributing factor. The stitching is also observed to be rolling over the edge of trim surfaces at corners, which the reviewer attributes to the stitch placement being too close to the edge. He notes that correcting this would have required repositioning the underlying surface, indicating a deeper design and manufacturing tradeoff that was not adequately resolved before production.

Notable quotes and data:
- "I'm seeing frayed threads through here... I'm questioning the quality of the thread that was used on the sewing process."
- "You'll see how it's just opening up a lot" — describing stitching behavior at curved trim corners.
- Reviewer notes the stitch "probably should have been sunk in a little bit farther" to prevent edge rollover.

2026-04-22.title: Daily X Summary (2026-04-22)
2026-04-22.body:
## Executive Summary
Today's posts were dominated by Tesla's unsupervised robotaxi operations continuing to expand (now operating in rain), an upcoming Q1 2026 earnings call with key investor questions around Optimus and autonomy, and a strong EV demand signal from California sales data. The overall tone is bullish, with autonomy momentum, institutional analyst support, and government fleet access providing multiple positive catalysts ahead of tomorrow's earnings call.

---

## Key Posts / Themes

1. **Unsupervised Robotaxi Operations Expand into Adverse Weather:** Tesla's unsupervised Model Y robotaxis were spotted operating in rainy conditions (post [7], 1.9K likes, 146 retweets — notable organic reach). This is a meaningful operational milestone, as adverse weather capability is one of the most-cited technical barriers to robotaxi scalability. No new cities or fleet size numbers were disclosed, but the footage signals expanding real-world operational envelope beyond ideal conditions.

2. **Q1 2026 Earnings Call Tomorrow — Key Investor Questions Flagged:** The earnings call is scheduled for Wednesday, April 23, 2026 (post [9]). Retail investor questions previewed include: (1) When will Optimus v3 be revealed and when does production start, given Model S/X production ended earlier than mid-year? (2) What is the expected Optimus production ramp? Additional questions likely touch on robotaxi expansion and FSD timelines. This is a high-priority catalyst window for TTT's core thesis variables.

3. **Model S/X Signature Edition Final Delivery Event — Factory Conversion Signal:** Tesla has announced an invite-only delivery event for the first of the final Model S and Model X Signature Edition vehicles on May 12th at the Fremont factory (post [1]). The framing as "last deliveries ever" and the earlier-than-midyear production end (referenced in post [9]) reinforces that Fremont capacity is being reallocated — likely toward Optimus manufacturing, consistent with prior guidance.

4. **EU Regulatory Engagement on FSD — Dutch Authority Extends Presentation:** The Dutch vehicle authority (RDW) has extended its May 5th presentation on Tesla FSD (Supervised) to the EU's Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) from 20 minutes to 1 hour (post [8]). Sawyer characterizes this as "only a good thing," suggesting deeper regulatory interest. The TCMV is a central body for EU vehicle approvals, making this a meaningful step toward potential European FSD authorization — a large addressable market currently inaccessible for FSD.

5. **Bank of America Reiterates Buy / $460 PT on Autonomy Thesis:** BofA analyst Alex Perry reiterated a Buy rating and $460 price target on TSLA, citing embedded robotaxi opportunity and Tesla being at the "early stages of monetization" of its autonomy capabilities as the key supporting factor (post [13]). No new financial model inputs were disclosed beyond the price target.

6. **Tesla Model Y Dominates California Q1 2026 Sales — #1 Overall Including ICE:** Tesla Model Y sold 22,907 units in California in Q1 2026, ranking #1 among all vehicles (EV and ICE), ahead of the Toyota Camry at 14,905 and Honda Civic at 12,806 (post [6]). This is a strong demand signal amid ongoing concerns about brand sentiment and macro headwinds, and demonstrates continued structural market leadership.

7. **Tesla Sourcewell Government Purchasing Agreement:** Tesla has entered a master purchasing agreement with Sourcewell, allowing U.S. government entities — cities, school districts, and state agencies — to purchase Tesla vehicles through a streamlined process (post [4], 1.4K likes, 156 retweets). This opens a new institutional demand channel and could accelerate fleet electrification adoption, with potential volume implications over time.

8. **Tesla Registers AI Voice Assistant with Chinese Authorities:** Tesla registered its generative AI-powered voice assistant with Shanghai's cyberspace administrator (post [5]). While incremental, regulatory registration is a prerequisite for broader AI feature deployment in China — Tesla's second-largest market — and signals continued progress navigating China's AI regulatory environment.

9. **Market & Competition — GM and VW Retreat from EVs:** General Motors is reportedly indefinitely delaying its next-generation full-size electric truck program, pivoting back to ICE and hybrid technology (post [2]). Separately, Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume announced plans to cut production capacity by an additional one million vehicles (post [14]). Both developments reduce competitive pressure on Tesla in key segments and reflect broader industry struggles with EV economics.

10. **CATL 3rd-Gen Shenxing LFP Battery — Competitive Battery Technology:** CATL unveiled its 3rd-generation Shenxing LFP battery with ultra-fast charging specs: 10%–35% in 1 minute, 10%–80% in 3 minutes 44 seconds, 10%–90% in 6.5 minutes, with performance maintained at -30°C (post [11], 4.3K likes — highest engagement of the day). While not directly a Tesla development, CATL is a key Tesla supplier, and this technology could eventually feed into Tesla's vehicle lineup. It also raises the competitive bar for charging speed across the industry.

---

## Signal Strength: **Bullish** — Unsupervised robotaxi operations demonstrating adverse-weather capability, a high-stakes earnings call tomorrow with autonomy/Optimus as focal points, strong California EV market leadership, expanding regulatory engagement in the EU, and institutional analyst support at $460 collectively reinforce the core TTT thesis ahead of a major catalyst event.

2026-04-23.title: Elon Musk Makes Big Tesla Predictions On Q1 2026 Earnings | Supercut
2026-04-23.body:
This video is a supercut of Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call, featuring opening remarks from Elon Musk and CFO Vaibhav Taneja, followed by Q&A with analysts and investors. The call covers Tesla's ambitious investment roadmap across autonomous driving, robotaxi expansion, Optimus humanoid robot production, chip development (AI5/Terafab), and energy storage — with Elon framing 2026 as a pivotal year of heavy capital deployment laying the groundwork for transformative future revenue streams.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD Version 14.3 as the architectural foundation:** Elon confirmed that FSD version 14.3 was a "major architectural update" and represents the last piece of the puzzle needed to enable unsupervised FSD. However, he noted the team is aware of additional major architectural improvements in the pipeline that would further improve safety, and Tesla does not intend to scale to very large unsupervised deployment until those improvements are written, validated, and released. Version 15 (V15) is targeted for later in 2026 or early 2027 and will be a "complete overhaul of the software architecture," running on AI4 hardware.

2. **Hardware 3 cannot support unsupervised FSD:** Elon explicitly stated that hardware 3 vehicles will never achieve unsupervised FSD capability, citing that hardware 3 has only one-eighth the memory bandwidth of hardware 4 — and memory bandwidth is described as the critical chokepoint for AI inference in autonomous driving. Tesla's solution is to offer discounted trade-ins toward hardware 4 vehicles and to offer hardware upgrades (requiring both computer and camera replacement). To execute this efficiently at scale, Tesla plans to set up "micro factories" or small facilities in major metropolitan areas rather than relying on slow service center throughput. The stated motivation is enabling hardware 3 owners to eventually enter the robotaxi fleet.

3. **Hardware 3 will receive a V14 distilled version:** An executive noted that a distilled version of V14 software will be released for hardware 3 vehicles, providing the same features as V14 for hardware 4, including starting drives from a parked state. This release is expected by the end of June 2026.

4. **AI4 Plus (AI4.1) upgrade planned:** Tesla is planning an upgrade to the current AI4 chip, moving from 16 GB to 32 GB of RAM per SOC (64 GB total), with approximately a 10% increase in compute and memory bandwidth. This updated chip, referred to as "AI4 Plus" or "AI4.1," is expected to go into production around mid-2027, dependent on Samsung completing the necessary modifications.

5. **FSD approved in Netherlands; EU-wide review expected:** FSD received regulatory approval in the Netherlands. The supervised FSD submission was expected to go to Brussels for EU-wide review in May 2026, with a broader EU approval potentially in Q2 2026. China FSD approval is being pursued with regulators, and Tesla hopes to receive it by Q3 2026. FSD paid customers reached nearly 1.3 million globally, with the bulk of growth from subscriptions. Churn rates are declining, indicating improving product satisfaction.

6. **FSD unsupervised release to customer cars expected in Q4 2026:** Elon said he expects unsupervised FSD to begin rolling out to the general customer fleet in Q4 2026, but the rollout will be gradual — geography by geography — as Tesla confirms each area is safe.

## Robotaxi

1. **Robotaxi operating in three cities with zero incidents:** Tesla's unsupervised robotaxi service is currently running in Austin, Dallas, and Houston, all using the same V14.3 software base deployed in the Bay Area. Elon emphasized that to date there have been zero accidents or injuries across the entire robotaxi program and described safety validation as the primary bottleneck for expansion, not technology readiness per se.

2. **Expansion target of roughly a dozen states by year-end:** Elon stated Tesla hopes to have unsupervised FSD or robotaxi operating in "a dozen or so states" by the end of 2026, with a cautious, validated rollout approach. He acknowledged robotaxi revenue will not be "super material" in 2026 but expects it to be "material in a significant way" in 2027.

3. **Operational challenges dominate over safety issues:** Elon and his team described the most common robotaxi operational problems as "convenience" issues rather than direct safety failures — including the vehicle getting "scared" to cross railroad tracks, getting stuck at permanently red lights, and literal infinite loops around construction zones. A specific anecdote was shared about a line of Tesla robotaxis blocked in a left-turn lane in Austin because a Waymo had crashed into a bus, preventing the lane from clearing. These edge cases are the primary focus of ongoing engineering work.

4. **QA fleet expanding across the US:** Tesla is growing its quality assurance fleet nationwide to accelerate safety validation. The team uses both real-world intervention data and neural network-based simulation to evaluate what would have happened in edge cases and makes expansion decisions based on those analyses.

5. **Robotaxi fleet growing quarter-over-quarter:** The CFO confirmed the robotaxi fleet grew quarter-over-quarter in Q1 2026 and that Tesla is making deliberate infrastructure investments to support further fleet growth and geographic expansion. Robotaxi revenue is currently captured under the Services and Other segment.

6. **Robotaxi strategy in Europe is premature:** Elon cautioned against expectations for a near-term robotaxi launch in Europe, noting that obtaining supervised FSD approval alone took an "immense amount of time." The timeline for unsupervised FSD or robotaxi approval in Europe is uncertain and dependent on regulators.

## Humanoid Bots

1. **Optimus V3 design nearly complete, reveal planned for mid-2026:** Elon said the Optimus V3 design is "almost ready to demonstrate," with some aesthetic elements still being finalized. He indicated a reveal is likely around mid-2026, though Tesla is deliberately delaying the public showing to prevent competitors from performing frame-by-frame analysis and copying the design — as has happened with previous Optimus unveils.

2. **Optimus production to begin at Fremont later in 2026:** Tesla is converting Fremont's Model S/X production line to Optimus manufacturing. The last Model S/X units will be produced in early May 2026, after which the final assembly line will be dismantled. Elon noted the full process — dismantling the existing line, installing the new Optimus line, wiring, commissioning — takes several months, and transitioning in approximately four months would be "an insanely fast speed" unprecedented in manufacturing. He estimated production start in the late July–August 2026 timeframe.

3. **Production ramp will be very slow initially:** Elon strongly cautioned against expecting significant Optimus output in 2026, explaining that with over 10,000 unique components, production speed is determined by "the least lucky, slowest, dumbest part." He described any near-term production rate prediction as "impossible" and said volume production would ramp meaningfully in 2027. Initial skills for factory-deployed Optimus will be simple tasks, building up from there.

4. **Second Optimus factory under construction at Giga Texas:** A second Optimus manufacturing facility is being constructed at the Giga Texas campus, expected to begin production around summer 2027.

5. **Optimus intelligence architecture — local plus cloud:** Elon described a hybrid intelligence model for Optimus: sufficient local on-board intelligence (similar to how Tesla cars operate without connectivity) to continue functioning if disconnected, combined with cloud-based orchestration via Grok for higher-level management and voice interaction. He characterized Grok's management role as analogous to a manager overseeing workers — Optimus could likely work for "several hours without any management oversight."

6. **Optimus remains Tesla's biggest product conviction:** Elon reiterated his view that Optimus will be "the biggest product ever" — not just Tesla's biggest, but in history — and that he remains "convinced of that conclusion." External Optimus deployment (outside Tesla) is tentatively targeted for sometime in 2027.

## Energy

1. **Q1 2026 energy storage deployment declined sequentially:** Tesla deployed 6.8 gigawatt-hours of energy storage in Q1 2026, a 38% sequential decline, described as consistent with the inherently "lumpy" nature of the business tied to customer deployment timelines. Despite the quarter's decline, management reiterated that full-year 2026 deployments are expected to exceed 2025 totals.

2. **Energy gross margins hit record 39.5% with one-time benefits:** The energy segment posted over 39.5% gross margin in Q1 2026, partly due to one-time tariff recognition benefits exceeding $250 million from tariffs paid in prior quarters. Management guided that margins will compress from this level due to increasing competition and ongoing tariff impacts on battery cells sourced from China.

3. **Megapack 3 production launch planned later in 2026:** Elon announced that Megapack 3 production will begin later in 2026 at a new factory outside Houston, described as a "world-class facility."

4. **Solar market in correction; Tesla launching lease product:** The US residential solar market is experiencing a downturn following the loss of the homeowner tax credit, but Tesla sees demand recovering in the second half of 2026. Tesla introduced a solar lease product this year to capture tax credits directly and offer competitive pricing to homeowners. Tesla also debuted its own solar panel and mounting system, creating a fully integrated home energy ecosystem.

## Electric Vehicles

1. **Demand resurgence in EMEA and Asia:** CFO Vaibhav Taneja noted over 150% quarter-over-quarter delivery growth in France and Germany in Q1 2026, and growth in South Korea and Japan. Even in the US, slight quarter-over-quarter delivery growth was observed. Tesla ended Q1 with its highest Q1 order backlog in over two years, with the improvement attributed partly to gas price increases but primarily to more compelling and affordable vehicles.

2. **Cybercab production has just started:** Elon confirmed that Cybercab production has just begun, describing it as early on the S-curve with very slow initial ramp expected, accelerating toward year-end and into 2027. He characterized Cybercab as a "compact two-person vehicle" and suggested it could eventually become the dominant vehicle in Tesla's lineup, since 90% of miles driven involve only one or two people.

3. **Semi-truck production starting soon:** Tesla Semi production is also beginning, with the same S-curve ramp dynamic expected — slow start, accelerating through year-end and into 2027.

4. **New Tesla Roadster debut potentially within a month:** Elon mentioned that the new Tesla Roadster could potentially be debuted "in a month or so," pending testing and validation to ensure a smooth demo. He described it as potentially "one of the most spectacular demos ever," though acknowledged it won't "move the needle massively" from a revenue standpoint.

5. **Battery pack capacity is the primary production constraint:** Management identified battery pack capacity — not cell supply per se — as the current main limiter on vehicle production. Remedies underway include: ramping in-house 4680 cells in Berlin (Model Y packs); retooling the Reno/Giga Nevada battery pack facility for more efficient output; and ramping in-house LFP module production in China.

6. **Giga Berlin set a record in Q1 2026:** Giga Berlin reached record output of over 61,000 units in Q1 2026, supported by the ramp of in-house 4680 battery packs for the Model Y.

7. **Autonomous vehicles to dominate future lineup:** Elon stated that long-term, almost the entire Tesla lineup will consist of autonomous vehicles of different sizes, with the only manually driven car being the new Tesla Roadster.

## Financials

1. **Automotive margins improved sequentially:** Auto gross margins excluding credits improved from 17.9% to 19.2% sequentially. The improvement included approximately $230 million in one-time warranty-related benefits. Tariffs and high interest rates continue to pressure automotive costs, with interest rate subvention costs recognized upfront.

2. **Capex guidance of over $25 billion for 2026:** Management guided to over $25 billion in capital expenditures for 2026, covering six factories moving toward operation, AI infrastructure for robotaxi and Optimus, the Terafab research semiconductor fab in Austin, and solar manufacturing equipment. Free cash flow ended Q1 at approximately $1.44 billion, and management explicitly warned of negative free cash flow for the remainder of 2026 due to this investment phase.

3. **FSD adoption approaching 1.3 million paid customers:** Tesla's FSD subscriber count reached nearly 1.3 million globally by Q1 2026, with most growth from subscriptions. Upfront FSD purchases grew only 7% after Tesla removed the purchase option in some markets. Subscriber churn is declining.

4. **Bitcoin mark-to-market and FX headwinds:** Net income was negatively impacted by mark-to-market losses on Bitcoin holdings (Bitcoin depreciated 22% in the quarter) and unfavorable foreign exchange impacts from large intercompany transactions.

5. **Services and Other margins improved:** The Services and Other segment gross margin improved from 8.8% to 9.2% sequentially, encompassing service centers, used cars, paid Supercharging, parts, insurance, and the emerging robotaxi business.

## Market & Competition

1. **Terafab: research fab at Giga Texas, SpaceX handling scaled fab:** Tesla plans to build a research semiconductor fabrication facility ("Terafab") on the Giga Texas campus, described as approximately a $3 billion initiative capable of producing a few thousand wafer starts per month. SpaceX will handle the initial phase of the larger-scale Terafab. Decisions require independent director review and board approval from both Tesla and SpaceX. Intel is partnering with Tesla to use Intel's 14A process technology, described as state-of-the-art.

2. **AI5 chip taped out early; AI6 and Dojo 3 in early stages:** The AI5 chip tape-out was completed ahead of schedule after six months of weekend and holiday work by the team. Elon called it "probably the best AI inference chip for edge compute that exists." AI5 is planned for Optimus and data centers, not immediately for vehicles, since AI4 is expected to be sufficient for unsupervised FSD well above human safety levels. Early momentum exists for designing AI6, and discussions about Dojo 3 have begun.

3. **Optimus competitors actively copying Tesla's designs:** Elon explicitly cited that competitors perform frame-by-frame analysis of every Optimus reveal and copy the design, which is the key reason Tesla is delaying the V3 reveal until closer to production start.

4. **Long-term chip supply is the core Terafab motivation:** Elon clarified that Terafab is not about gaining negotiating leverage over chip suppliers, but about ensuring Tesla has access to sufficient AI chip supply as it scales — noting the industry's production growth rate for both logic and memory chips cannot keep pace with Tesla's projected needs, particularly if AI satellites or similar deployments become reality.

---

**Notable quotes and data:**

- *"I think Optimus will be our biggest product, not just Tesla's biggest product ever, but probably the biggest product ever."* — Elon Musk
- *"If we're able to go from stopping production on one line, dismantling that entire line, reinstalling a whole new line, and turning that on in a matter of 4 months, that is an insanely fast speed. I don't think any other company on Earth has ever done that before."* — Elon Musk
- *"14.3 is the last piece of the puzzle for unsupervised FSD."* — Elon Musk
- *"Hardware 3 has only 1/8 of the memory bandwidth of hardware 4."* — Elon Musk
- *"We haven't had any injuries and certainly no fatalities to date with the unsupervised FSD and robotaxi expansion."* — Elon Musk
- *"We certainly hope to have unsupervised FSD or robotaxi operating in a dozen or so states by the end of this year."* — Elon Musk
- *"Unsupervised FSD or robotaxi revenue will not be super material this year, but it will be material — probably in a significant way — next year."* — Elon Musk
- Giga Berlin record output: **61,000+ units** in Q1 2026
- Energy storage deployed in Q1 2026: **6.8 GWh** (down 38% sequentially)
- Energy gross margin Q1 2026: **over 39.5%** (includes ~$250M one-time tariff benefit)
- Auto gross margin ex-credits: improved from **17.9% to 19.2%**
- FSD paid customers: **nearly 1.3 million globally**
- 2026 capex guidance: **over $25 billion**
- Free cash flow end of Q1: **~$1.44 billion**
- Warranty one-time benefit: **~$230 million**
- AI4 Plus: **16 GB → 32 GB RAM per SOC (64 GB total)**, ~10% compute increase, targeting mid-2027 production
- Terafab research fab: **~$3 billion** initiative, **few thousand wafer starts/month**, using **Intel 14A process**
- V14 for hardware 3: expected **end of June 2026**
- Unsupervised FSD to customer cars: **expected Q4 2026**
- Optimus V3 reveal: **approximately mid-2026**
- Optimus Fremont production start: **late July–August 2026 timeframe**
- Second Optimus factory (Giga Texas): **production expected around summer 2027**

2026-04-23.title: Tesla Earnings Call Confused Investors? Here’s Why!
2026-04-23.body:
This video from the "brighterwithherbert" channel features host Herbert and Tesla journalist Brian White (of the YouTube channel Futurasa) analyzing the Tesla Q1 2026 earnings call, which many investors found confusing or discouraging. The core argument is that the negative reaction was driven largely by Elon Musk's tone rather than the substance of what was announced, and that the actual content — on Cybercab production, FSD adoption, and robotaxi expansion — was broadly positive. The hosts walk through key audio clips from the call to clarify what was and wasn't actually said about delays and timelines.

## Electric Vehicles
1. **Cybercab enters production at Giga Texas:** Tesla officially announced that Cybercab production has begun at Giga Texas. Elon Musk cautioned that, as with any new product involving a completely new supply chain, the initial production will follow a slow S-curve before ramping exponentially toward the end of 2026 and into 2027. Tesla's earnings deck confirmed that Cybercab, Tesla Semi, and Megapack 3 are all on schedule for volume production starting in 2026.

2. **Cybercab to eventually replace the Model Y as Tesla's highest-volume vehicle:** Tesla confirmed in their earnings deck that once in production, they expect the Cybercab to begin replacing the existing Model Y fleet and to become the largest-volume vehicle in the fleet over time. Elon has also reiterated that eventually 90% of all Tesla vehicles will be Cybercabs, with the only driver-operable vehicle being the Roadster.

3. **Tesla Semi production ramp also underway:** Tesla Semi production has not yet formally begun, but Elon confirmed it is starting soon. Brian White noted the Semi has accumulated enough road miles for Tesla to be confident in proceeding, though the 4680 battery supply — given that each Semi requires the equivalent of 10–12 cars' worth of batteries — may be a remaining bottleneck. Tesla Semi is priced approximately 40% below competing electric semi offerings, making it highly competitive.

4. **Hardware 3 cannot achieve unsupervised FSD:** Elon confirmed that Hardware 3 vehicles are not capable of running unsupervised FSD. Tesla is offering two remedies: a discounted trade-in for customers who want to upgrade to an AI4-equipped vehicle, and the ability to upgrade the car's computer and cameras in place. Elon noted that to do this efficiently, Tesla will need to set up micro-factories or small factories in major metropolitan areas, as service center upgrades would be too slow and inefficient. He indicated it would eventually make sense to convert all Hardware 3 cars to Hardware 4, enabling them to join the robotaxi fleet. A limited "FSD version 14 light" for Hardware 3 cars is planned for release in June 2026, which will be supervised-only but functionally close to version 14 for most point-to-point trips.

5. **Inventory and EV demand tailwinds:** Brian White noted Tesla currently sits at approximately 27 days of inventory, which he views as well-timed given rising global gas prices that may push more consumers toward EVs. He also noted that in the UK, EVs are already cheaper to operate than petrol alternatives.

## Autonomous Driving
1. **FSD adoption accelerating sharply — 28.8 million miles per day:** Tesla's FSD fleet is now driving an average of 28.8 million miles per day, up from 14.4 million just a couple of months ago — a doubling in a very short period. The hosts note this equates to roughly 1,000 miles every 3 seconds across the fleet.

2. **FSD subscription take rate exceeding 50% on new deliveries:** Analyst Cern compiled data showing that the incremental FSD take rate — defined as the change in active paid FSD subscriptions over incremental deliveries in the most recent quarter — has now exceeded 50%. This figure explicitly excludes free trials. The quarter-over-quarter increase in subscriptions was approximately 170,000, equating to roughly $16.8 million per month or $50 million per quarter in additional revenue just from the increase. Total FSD revenue including upfront purchases is estimated at approximately $375 million per quarter, described as essentially pure margin.

3. **FSD version 15 confirmed for AI4 hardware — targeting end of 2026:** Elon confirmed that FSD version 15 will run on AI4 hardware. He described version 15 as a complete overhaul of the software architecture, intended to enable unsupervised FSD anywhere in the world where it is legally permitted. He said this version will "hopefully" be available by the end of 2026. Both hosts are currently running FSD version 14.2, which they describe as extremely close to a comfort level suitable for unsupervised use, with Brian citing a drive to California at over 98% FSD engagement.

4. **FSD version 14.3 is the current ceiling — a newer architecture needed before global scale:** Elon stated that FSD version 14.3 represents the last piece of the puzzle for the current software generation, but that there are known major architectural improvements that would significantly improve safety. He indicated it would not make sense to deploy unsupervised FSD or robotaxi at large scale while those known improvements remain unimplemented. The hosts debated whether this implied a wait until version 15, or whether it only referred to truly global scale — concluding that expansion to a dozen states can proceed on the current trajectory while version 15 is developed.

5. **AI4 confirmed sufficient for unsupervised FSD; AI5 going to Optimus first:** Elon confirmed that AI4 hardware is sufficient to achieve unsupervised FSD and that there is no pressing need to move to AI5 in cars. AI5 will go into Optimus first, and it may be some time before it reaches vehicles. An "AI4 Plus" variant — featuring upgraded RAM (from 16 GB to 32 GB per chip, or 64 GB in the dual configuration) and approximately a 10% increase in compute — is planned to go into production in mid-2027, contingent on Samsung's manufacturing capability.

## Robotaxi
1. **Robotaxi targeting a dozen or so states by end of 2026:** Elon said he expects unsupervised FSD or robotaxi to be operating in "a dozen or so states" by the end of 2026. He noted Tesla has had no injuries and no fatalities with unsupervised FSD and robotaxi to date, and that Tesla is taking a cautious rollout approach to maintain that record.

2. **Robotaxi revenue will be material but not "super material" in 2026 — significant in 2027:** Elon stated that unsupervised FSD and robotaxi revenue will be material in 2026, but not "super material." He expects it to be material "in a significant way" in 2027. Brian White interpreted this as the revenue in 2026 not being sufficient to offset the infrastructure, operations, insurance, and buildout costs incurred to date — meaning the net financial impact won't be clearly positive until 2027.

3. **The "delay" debate — scale vs. global expansion:** A central debate among investors following the earnings call was whether Elon's comments meant robotaxi was delayed. The hosts' interpretation is that it was not delayed for near-term U.S. multi-state rollout, but that "large scale" in Elon's framing likely means global or near-universal deployment — not the initial dozen-state expansion. The Cybercab production ramp, even at its initially slow pace (hundreds of units per week in the early weeks), means unsupervised robotaxis will be operating in meaningful numbers well before FSD version 15 is released.

4. **Operational challenges are now the main barrier — not safety:** The hosts emphasize Elon's framing that the barrier to wide-scale robotaxi deployment is now operational, not safety. Key operational issues cited include edge cases like a bus blocking a lane that causes the fleet to stall — situations requiring remote operator intervention. The ratio of remote operators to vehicles was raised as an open question. Elon also described an "infinite loop" problem where vehicles sit idle rather than route around obstacles, which needs to be solved before broader scale.

## Market & Competition
1. **Cybercab unit volumes will dwarf current EV competitors from day one:** Brian White noted that even a painfully slow Cybercab ramp of hundreds or a few thousand units per week will likely outsell many of Tesla's competitors who periodically announce "strong months" with much smaller volumes. He drew the comparison to Model Y production in Shanghai, where Tesla quickly localized and scaled its supply chain under factory leadership.

Notable quotes and data:
- Elon Musk: "Unsupervised FSD or robotaxi operating in, I don't know, a dozen or so states by the end of this year."
- Elon Musk: "I think probably unsupervised FSD or robotaxi revenue will not be super material this year, but I do think it will be material. It'll be material probably in a significant way next year."
- Elon Musk: "I think it's not going to make sense for us to deploy unsupervised FSD or robotaxi at large scale when we know that there are major architectural improvements to the software that can improve safety."
- Elon Musk on Hardware 3 upgrades: "We're going to have to set up like kind of micro-factories or small factories in major metropolitan areas in order to do it efficiently."
- Tesla earnings deck: "Cybercab, Tesla Semi, and Megapack 3 are on schedule for volume production starting in 2026."
- Tesla earnings deck: "First generation production lines for Optimus are being installed in anticipation of volume production."
- Tesla earnings deck: "We expect the Cybercab will begin to replace the existing Model Y fleet and will be the largest vehicle in the fleet over time."
- FSD daily miles: 28.8 million miles/day, up from 14.4 million — a doubling in a few months
- Incremental FSD paid subscription increase last quarter: ~170,000 subscribers
- Additional FSD subscription revenue from the increase alone: ~$16.8 million/month, ~$50 million/quarter
- Total FSD revenue estimate (including upfront purchases): ~$375 million/quarter described as "essentially pure margin"
- AI4 Plus specs: 32 GB RAM per chip (64 GB dual), ~10% compute increase, targeted for mid-2027 production
- FSD version 14 light for Hardware 3 cars: targeted for June 2026, supervised-only
- Brian White personal FSD experience: over 98% engagement rate on a long drive to California on version 14.2
- Current Tesla inventory: approximately 27 days

2026-04-23.title: The Tesla Earnings Call Wall Street Misread
2026-04-23.body:
This video features host Herbert interviewing Larry Goldberg, a serial entrepreneur and venture capital investor, analyzing Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call and why Wall Street's negative reaction to the capex increase was misguided. The core thesis is that Tesla's decision to raise 2026 capital expenditure from $20 billion to $25 billion — combined with announcements around a research chip fab at Giga Texas, Dojo 3, and a new AI hardware acquisition — signals aggressive investment in physical AI, not financial distress. The hosts argue the market is applying the wrong framework to Tesla, penalizing it for spending that would be celebrated in pure-play AI companies.

## Financials

1. **Capex Raise Misread by Wall Street:** Tesla announced it is raising 2026 capital expenditure from $20 billion to $25 billion — a 25% step-up in a single quarter. Wall Street interpreted this as a sign of spending out of control and sold the stock, which swung from up $15 to sharply negative during the earnings call. Both the host and Larry Goldberg argue this reaction is wrong and that the capex increase should be read as growth investment, not maintenance spending. Bill Ackman was cited agreeing with this interpretation, distinguishing between maintenance capex (which should cause concern if rising) and growth capex (which investors should applaud).

2. **Q1 Capex Underspend and Implied Acceleration:** Tesla only spent $2.5 billion in capex in Q1 2026, meaning they were already behind pace relative to their original $20 billion annual target before the raise was announced. Goldberg argues this means the actual rate of spending acceleration through the rest of the year will be very steep. He also notes Tesla historically has not fully spent its announced capex budgets, and expresses skepticism they will reach the full $25 billion this year — though he expects them to commit to it.

3. **Free Cash Flow Goes Negative — But That's Acceptable:** Tesla reported $1.7 billion in free cash flow for Q1 2026, which surprised many investors. Both hosts say they expect free cash flow to go negative for the next several quarters given the capex ramp, and view this as acceptable as long as the company remains operationally profitable. Tesla is described as sitting on $45 billion in cash, self-funding its AI buildout without tapping shareholders.

4. **Auto Gross Margin Beat:** Auto gross margin came in at 19.2% excluding credits, or above 20% including credits — well ahead of analyst estimates of 17.5% to 17.9%. This was highlighted by Gene Munster as a significant positive that the market's focus on capex overshadowed.

5. **Tax Write-Off Advantage:** Goldberg notes that 2026 is the first year companies can write off all capex on plant, equipment, and buildings, meaning Tesla's aggressive spending this year also provides an enormous tax benefit — making the timing of the investment even more strategically sound.

6. **AI Hardware Acquisition Disclosed in 10-Q:** Tesla's newly filed 10-Q revealed an acquisition in the AI hardware space. Goldberg initially cited it as approximately $1.5 billion (with some uncertainty about whether it was $2 billion), and described it as contributing to the capex jump. He views this as Tesla "bulking up" its AI hardware capabilities.

7. **Capex Trajectory Projections:** Gene Munster projected Tesla's capex will continue rising in 2027 and estimated approximately $40 billion for next year. Goldberg goes further, predicting Tesla will peak at $70 billion in annual capex — more than double the current 2026 level — citing the Terafab buildout, AI infrastructure needs, and the AI hardware acquisition as key drivers.

8. **Energy Revenue Down — A Concern:** Goldberg flags that energy revenue was down in Q1 2026 and that the 10-Q attributed this to tariffs and competition rather than a large volume of work-in-progress, which had been his initial expectation. He describes this as a negative data point in an otherwise positive financial report.

## Autonomous Driving

1. **FSD Version 14.3 as the Capability Milestone:** Elon Musk stated on the earnings call that FSD version 14.3 is "the last piece of the puzzle" for unsupervised capability, but that improvements still need to be made before going to full scale. Goldberg and the host interpret this to mean 14.3 is sufficient to begin unsupervised operations at limited scale, and that waiting for version 15 is not required to get started — version 15 would represent a further leap but is not a prerequisite.

2. **FSD Beginning to Generate Real Revenue:** Goldberg notes the earnings results showed FSD beginning to pay "real dividends" and generate real income, marking a meaningful milestone in monetization of the autonomous driving software stack.

3. **12 States by End of 2026:** Elon stated on the call that Tesla expects to have unsupervised FSD operations across 12 states by the end of 2026, which the hosts cite as evidence there is no fundamental delay to the robotaxi rollout — only a measured, safety-first ramp.

## Robotaxi

1. **No Meaningful Earnings Until Mid-2027:** Elon Musk stated on the earnings call that robotaxi earnings should not be expected to be meaningful until next year (i.e., mid-2027).
